title.zh: 卷七十二 志第二十三: 祭祀一
title.raw: 卷七十二 志第二十三: 祭祀一 Volume 72 Treatises 25: Offerings 1

sentences.zh: 祭祀一

translations.literal: Sacrificial Offerings I
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial Offerings, Part One

sentences.zh: 禮之有祭祀，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: In ritual, there being sacrificial offerings—this goes back to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice as part of ritual reaches far back into antiquity.

sentences.zh: 天子者，天地宗廟社稷之主，於郊社禘嘗有事守焉，以其義存乎報本，非有所為而為之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven is lord of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; at suburban altars, communal altars, di and chang rites there are duties to uphold, because the meaning lies in repaying origins—not done for ulterior motives.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is master of heaven and earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain. Suburban rites, communal offerings, and the great di and chang sacrifices all demand his attentive duty, for their meaning is to repay one's origins—not to be performed with ulterior motives.

sentences.zh: 故其禮貴誠而尚質，務在反本循古，不忘其初而已。

translations.literal: Therefore in their rites sincerity is prized and simplicity esteemed; the aim is to return to origins, follow antiquity, and not forget the beginning—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Hence these rites prize sincerity and simplicity, seeking only to return to roots, follow ancient ways, and never forget beginnings.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦弊，郊廟之制，置《周禮》不用，謀議巡守封禪，而方士祠官之說興，兄弟相繼共為一代，而統緒亂。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin's defects; in suburban and temple systems they set aside the Rites of Zhou unused, deliberated on imperial tours and feng and shan sacrifices, while theories of wonder-workers and sacrificial officials arose; brothers succeeded one another jointly as one generation, and the succession lineage was disordered.
translations.idiomatic: The Han inherited Qin's decay: suburban and temple ritual discarded the Rites of Zhou, court debate turned to imperial tours and feng and shan sacrifices, and the claims of wonder-workers and sacrificial officers flourished. Brothers ruled in succession as if one generation, and the royal line fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 迨其季世，乃合南北二郊為一。

translations.literal: By their closing age, they combined the southern and northern suburban altars into one.
translations.idiomatic: Only in its late years did the dynasty merge the southern and northern suburban altars into one.

sentences.zh: 雖以唐、宋盛時，亦莫之正，蓋未有能反其本而求之者。

translations.literal: Even in the flourishing ages of Tang and Song, no one corrected this; presumably none could return to the root and seek it.
translations.idiomatic: Even Tang and Song at their height never set this right—there was no one who could return to the root and seek the original form.

sentences.zh: 彼籩豆之事，有司所職，又豈足以盡仁人孝子之心哉！

translations.literal: Those matters of baskets and stands are the duties of clerks—how could they suffice to fulfill the hearts of humane persons and filial children!
translations.idiomatic: The details of baskets and stands belong to minor officials—how could they ever fulfill the heart of the truly humane and filial!

sentences.zh: 元之五禮，皆以國俗行之，惟祭祀稍稽諸古。

translations.literal: Of the Yuan's five rites, all were conducted according to national customs; only sacrificial offerings slightly examined antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan conducted all five categories of ritual by national custom; only in sacrifice did they look somewhat to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其郊廟之儀，禮官所考日益詳慎，而舊禮初未嘗廢，豈亦所謂不忘其初者歟？

translations.literal: In suburban and temple ceremonies, what rites officials investigated grew daily more detailed and careful, yet the old rites were never abandoned at the start—is this not what is called not forgetting the beginning?
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple ritual grew ever more minutely prescribed by the rites officials, yet the old customs were never cast aside from the start—is this not, after all, the meaning of "not forgetting beginnings"?

sentences.zh: 然自世祖以來，每難於親其事。

translations.literal: Yet from Shizu onward, each time it was difficult to personally perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Emperor Shizu onward, emperors found it difficult to perform these rites in person.

sentences.zh: 英宗始有意親郊，而誌弗克遂。

translations.literal: Yingzong first intended to personally perform suburban sacrifice, but his intent could not be realized.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong first resolved to sacrifice at the suburban altar in person, but the plan never came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 久之，其禮乃成於文宗。

translations.literal: After a long time, the rite was finally accomplished under Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later was the rite finally completed under Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 至大間，大臣議立北郊而中輟，遂廢不講。

translations.literal: During the Zhida reign, grand ministers deliberated on establishing the northern suburban altar but stopped midway, and it was abandoned without further discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhida era ministers debated establishing a northern suburban altar, but the project halted halfway and was abandoned without further discussion.

sentences.zh: 然武宗親享於廟者三，英宗親享五。

translations.literal: Yet Wuzong personally offered at the temple three times; Yingzong personally offered five times.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong nonetheless attended the temple in person three times; Yingzong, five.

sentences.zh: 晉王在帝位四年矣，未嘗一廟見。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin had been on the throne four years, yet had never once appeared at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin reigned four years without once attending the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 文宗以後，乃復親享。

translations.literal: After Wenzong, personal offering was again resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Wenzong did emperors again sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 豈以道釋禱祠薦禳之盛，竭生民之力以營寺宇者，前代所未有，有所重則有所輕歟。

translations.literal: Was it because Daoist and Buddhist prayer-offerings, presentation rites, and exorcisms flourished, exhausting the people's strength to build temples—something no prior age had had—so that what was emphasized, something else was slighted?
translations.idiomatic: Was it because Daoist and Buddhist prayer, presentation, and exorcism rites grew so lavish—draining the people's strength to build temples as no prior age had done—that what was emphasized left something else neglected?

sentences.zh: 或曰，北陲之俗，敬天而畏鬼，其巫祝每以為能親見所祭者，而知其喜怒，故天子非有察於幽明之故、禮俗之辨，則未能親格，豈其然歟？

translations.literal: Some say: the customs of the northern frontier honor heaven and fear ghosts; their shamans and invokers often claim they can personally see the object of sacrifice and know its joy and anger—therefore unless the Son of Heaven has insight into causes of the hidden and manifest and distinctions of ritual and custom, he cannot personally approach—can this be so?
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that frontier peoples revere heaven and fear ghosts, and that their shamans claim to see the spirits offered to and read their moods; only a Son of Heaven who truly understands the divide between visible and invisible realms and between ritual and custom could personally approach the gods—is this truly the reason?

sentences.zh: 自憲宗祭天日月山，追崇所生與太祖並配，世祖所建太廟，皇伯術赤、察合帶皆以家人禮祔於列室。

translations.literal: Since Möngke sacrificed to heaven at Sun-and-Moon Mountain, raising his biological parent to share sacrifice with Taizu; in the Grand Temple Shizu built, Imperial Uncles Jochi and Chagatai were both enshrined in side chambers by family rites.
translations.idiomatic: From Möngke's sacrifice to heaven at Sun-and-Moon Mountain, when he honored his birth parent to share the altar with Taizu, through the Grand Temple Shizu erected—Imperial Uncles Jochi and Chagatai were both installed in side chambers by family rite.

sentences.zh: 既而太宗、定宗以世天下之君俱不獲廟享，而憲宗亦以不祀。

translations.literal: Subsequently Ögedei and Dingzong, as worldly rulers of all under Heaven, both failed to receive temple enjoyment; and Möngke likewise went without sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ögedei and Dingzong, as rulers of the realm, never received temple sacrifices; Möngke likewise went unhonored.

sentences.zh: 則其因襲之弊，蓋有非禮官之議所能及者。

translations.literal: Then the defects of inherited practice were surely beyond what rites officials' deliberations could reach.
translations.idiomatic: The defects of inherited practice lay beyond anything rites officials could deliberate away.

sentences.zh: 而況乎不禰所受國之君，而兄弟共為一世，乃有征於前代者歟？

translations.literal: Moreover—not enshrining the lord who received the state, while brothers jointly count as one generation—was there not precedent in former ages?
translations.idiomatic: And when the ruler who actually received the mandate was not given main enshrinement while brothers were counted as one generation together—had this not happened before?

sentences.zh: 夫郊廟，國之大祀也，本原之際既已如此，則中祀以下，雖有闊略，無足言者。

translations.literal: Suburban altars and temples are the state's greatest sacrifices; since at the very root it was already thus, then middle sacrifices and below—even if broad or abbreviated—are not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altars and the ancestral temple are the state's greatest sacrifices. When the foundation itself was so flawed, minor and middle rites—however lax—hardly merit discussion.

sentences.zh: 其天子親遣使致祭者三：曰社稷，曰先農，曰宣聖。

translations.literal: Those for which the Son of Heaven personally dispatched envoys to offer sacrifice were three: the altars of soil and grain, the First Farmer, and the Exalted Sage.
translations.idiomatic: Three received envoys sent by the Son of Heaven in person: the altars of soil and grain, the First Farmer, and Confucius the Exalted Sage.

sentences.zh: 而嶽鎮海瀆，使者奉璽書即其處行事，稱代祀。

translations.literal: For mounts, peaks, seas, and rivers, envoys bearing imperial writ performed rites on site; this was called proxy sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For the sacred mountains, seas, and rivers, envoys bearing the imperial seal performed the rite on the spot—called proxy sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其有司常祀者五：曰社稷，曰宣聖，曰三皇，曰嶽鎮海瀆，曰風師雨師。

translations.literal: Those with regular sacrifice by officials were five: soil and grain altars, Exalted Sage, Three Sovereigns, mounts peaks seas and rivers, and masters of wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Five received regular sacrifice by officials: soil and grain, the Exalted Sage, the Three Sovereigns, sacred mountains and rivers, and the masters of wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 其非通祀者五：曰武成王，曰古帝王廟，曰周公廟，曰名山大川、忠臣義士之祠，曰功臣之祠，而大臣家廟不與焉。

translations.literal: Non-universal sacrifices were five: King Wu Cheng, ancient emperors' temples, Duke of Zhou's temple, famous mountains and rivers and loyal ministers' shrines, meritorious officials' shrines—grand ministers' family temples were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Five were not universal sacrifices: King Wu Cheng, temples of ancient emperors, the Duke of Zhou, shrines to famous mountains and loyal martyrs, and shrines to meritorious officials—family temples of grand ministers were excluded.

sentences.zh: 其儀皆禮官所擬，而議定於中書。

translations.literal: Their ceremonies were all drafted by rites officials and decided by the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials drafted every ceremony; the Secretariat made the final decision.

sentences.zh: 日星始祭於司天臺，而回回司天臺遂以翙星為職事。

translations.literal: Sun and stars were first offered at the Bureau of Astronomy; then the Muslim Bureau of Astronomy took cometary observation as its duty.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and stars were first worshipped at the Astronomical Bureau; the Muslim astronomical bureau later made cometary observation its particular charge.

sentences.zh: 五福太乙有壇畤，以道流主之，皆所未詳。

translations.literal: Five Blessings and Taiyi had altars, administered by Daoist clergy—all unclear in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Altars to the Five Blessings and Taiyi were overseen by Daoist clergy—matters little documented.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀之事，其書為《太常集禮》，而《經世大典》之《禮典篇》尤備。

translations.literal: For all sacrificial matters the book was Collected Rites of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, while the Ritual Canon section of the Institutions for an Age was especially complete.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial matters were recorded in Collected Rites of the Grand Master of Ceremonies; the Ritual Canon in Institutions for an Age was especially comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 參以累朝《實錄》與《六條政類》，序其因革，錄其成制，作《祭祀志》。

translations.literal: Referencing successive reigns' Veritable Records and Six Categories of Governance, ordering their changes and reforms, recording their established institutions—thus this Treatise on Sacrificial Offerings was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on successive Veritable Records and the Six Categories of Governance, this treatise records reforms and established forms—the Treatise on Sacrificial Offerings.

sentences.zh: ○郊祀上

translations.literal: ○ Suburban Sacrifice, Part One
translations.idiomatic: ○ Suburban Sacrifice, Part One

sentences.zh: 元與朔漠，代有拜天之禮，衣冠尚質，祭器尚純，帝後親之，宗戚助祭。

translations.literal: The Yuan arose from the northern deserts; generation after generation had the rite of worshipping heaven; dress and caps prized simplicity, vessels purity; emperor and empress personally attended, kin assisted.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan rose from the northern steppe, where each generation worshipped heaven: dress was plain, vessels unadorned, emperor and empress attended in person, and kinsmen assisted at the altar.

sentences.zh: 其意幽深玄遠，報本反始，出於自然，而非強為之也。

translations.literal: Its intent was profound and abstruse, repaying origins and returning to beginnings, arising naturally—not forced.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning was profound and primal: repaying origins and returning to beginnings, arising naturally rather than by compulsion.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位之二年秋八月八日，始以冕服拜天於日月山。

translations.literal: Second year autumn, eighth month, eighth day after Möngke's accession—first wearing ceremonial cap and robes to worship heaven at Sun-and-Moon Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the second year of Möngke's reign, he first worshipped heaven at Sun-and-Moon Mountain in full ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 其十二日，又用孔氏子孫元措言，合祭昊天后土，始大合樂作牌位，以太祖、睿宗配享。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day, again following Kong clan descendant Yuan Cuo's words, jointly sacrificed to August Heaven and Queen Earth; first used full music and made spirit tablets—Taizu and Ruizong as associated enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth, following Kong descendant Yuan Cuo, he jointly sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, first assembling full music and spirit tablets, with Taizu and Ruizong as associated spirits.

sentences.zh: 歲甲寅，會諸王於顆顆腦兒之西，丁巳秋，駐蹕於軍腦兒，皆祭天於其地。

translations.literal: Year jiayin, assembled princes west of Köke Nuur; dingsi autumn, encamped at Khüri Nuur—all sacrificed to heaven at those places.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiayin year princes gathered west of Köke Nuur; in the dingsi autumn the court halted at Khüri Nuur—at both places heaven was worshipped.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年，親征北方。

translations.literal: Shizu, second year of Zhongtong—personally campaigned north.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong, Shizu campaigned north in person.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己亥，躬祀天於舊桓州之西北，灑馬湩以為禮，皇族之外無得而與，皆如其初。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month jihai—personally sacrificed to heaven northwest of old Huanzhou; sprinkling kumiss as the rite; beyond the imperial clan none could participate—all as at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the fourth month of summer he sacrificed to heaven northwest of old Huanzhou, sprinkling kumiss as the offering; none outside the imperial clan shared the rite—all as in the beginning.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年十二月，以受尊號，遣使豫告天地，下太常檢討唐、宋、金舊儀，於國陽麗正門東南七里建祭臺，設昊天上帝、皇地祇位二，行一獻禮。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, twelfth year of Zhiyuan—upon receiving the honorific title, dispatched envoys to announce in advance to Heaven and Earth; ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to examine Tang, Song, and Jin old rites; built a sacrificial platform seven li southeast of the Guoyang Lizheng Gate, set two positions for August Heaven and Queen Earth, performed one presentation rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, upon receiving his honorific title, he sent envoys to announce the event to Heaven and Earth in advance. The Grand Master of Ceremonies was ordered to review Tang, Song, and Jin precedents. A sacrificial platform was built seven li southeast of the Guoyang Lizheng Gate, with places for August Heaven and Queen Earth, and a single presentation was offered.

sentences.zh: 自後國有大典禮，皆即南郊告謝焉。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the state had a great ceremony, all announced thanks at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every major state ceremony was announced and thanked at the southern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，以平宋，遣使告天地，中書下太常議定儀物以聞。

translations.literal: Fifth month, thirteenth year—upon pacifying Song, dispatched envoys to announce to Heaven and Earth; the Secretariat ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to deliberate and fix ritual objects and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, after the conquest of Song, envoys announced the victory to Heaven and Earth; the Secretariat ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to settle the ritual objects and report.

sentences.zh: 制若曰：「其以國禮行事。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Let it be conducted according to national rites."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Conduct it according to national rite."

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位。

translations.literal: Thirty-first year—Chengzong acceded.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Chengzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬寅，始為壇於都城南七里。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month renyin—first built an altar seven li south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the fourth month of summer the first altar was built seven li south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遣司徒兀都帶率百官為大行皇帝請謚南郊，為告天請謚之始。

translations.literal: Jiachen—dispatched Grand Mentor Oqtay leading all officials to request a posthumous title for the late emperor at the southern suburban altar; this was the beginning of announcing to heaven to request a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Grand Mentor Oqtay was sent with the full bureaucracy to the southern suburban altar to seek a posthumous title for the late emperor—the first such announcement to heaven for a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 大德六年春三月庚戌，合祭昊天上帝、皇地祇、五方帝於南郊，遣左丞相哈剌哈孫攝事，為攝祀天地之始。

translations.literal: Third month gengxu, spring sixth year of Dade—jointly sacrificed to August Heaven, Queen Earth, and Five Directional Emperors at the southern suburban altar; dispatched Left Chancellor Qarachar to preside by proxy; this was the beginning of proxy sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day in the third month of spring in the sixth year of Dade, August Heaven, Queen Earth, and the Five Directional Emperors were jointly sacrificed to at the southern suburban altar; Left Chancellor Qarachar was sent to preside by proxy—the first proxy sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 大德九年二月二十四日，右丞相哈剌哈孫等言：「去年地震星變，雨澤愆期，歲比不登。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth day, second month, ninth year of Dade—Right Chancellor Qarachar and others said: "Last year there were earthquakes and stellar anomalies; rain and dew were untimely; harvests failed year after year.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of the second month in the ninth year of Dade, Right Chancellor Qarachar and others said: "Last year brought earthquakes and strange stars in the sky; rain came late; harvests failed year after year.

sentences.zh: 祈天保民之事，有天子親祀者三：曰天，曰祖宗，曰社稷。

translations.literal: Matters of praying to heaven to protect the people that the Son of Heaven personally sacrifices to are three: heaven, ancestors, and soil and grain altars.
translations.idiomatic: Three matters require the Son of Heaven's personal prayer to heaven for the people's welfare: heaven, the ancestors, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟、社稷，歲時攝官行事。

translations.literal: Now for ancestral temple and soil and grain altars, each year proxy officials perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain are already served each year by proxy officials.

sentences.zh: 祭天，國之大事也，陛下雖未及親祀，宜如宗廟、社稷，遣官攝祭，歲用冬至，儀物有司豫備，日期至則以聞。」

translations.literal: Sacrifice to heaven is a great affair of state; though Your Majesty has not yet been able to sacrifice in person, it is fitting, as with ancestral temple and soil and grain altars, to dispatch officials to sacrifice by proxy, using the winter solstice each year; ritual objects should be prepared in advance by the relevant offices, and when the date arrives it should be reported."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to heaven is a matter of the highest state importance. Though Your Majesty has not yet been able to attend in person, you should follow the precedent of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain: dispatch officials to sacrifice by proxy at the winter solstice each year, have the relevant offices prepare the ritual objects in advance, and report when the day arrives."

sentences.zh: 制若曰：「卿言是也，其豫備儀物以待事。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your words are correct; prepare the ritual objects in advance to await the affair."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "You are right. Prepare the ritual objects in advance for the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 於是翰林、集賢、太常禮官皆會中書集議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hanlin, Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and Grand Master of Ceremonies rites officials all met at the Secretariat for collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon rites officials from the Hanlin Academy, the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and the Grand Master of Ceremonies all assembled at the Secretariat for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 博士疏曰：「冬至，圜丘惟祀昊天上帝，至西漢元始間，始合祭天地。

translations.literal: A erudite submitted: "At the winter solstice, the round mound altar sacrifices only to August Heaven; only by the Yuanshi reign of Western Han did joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth begin.
translations.idiomatic: An erudite submitted: "At the winter solstice the round mound altar sacrifices only to August Heaven. Joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth did not begin until the Yuanshi reign of Western Han.

sentences.zh: 歷東漢至宋千有餘年，分祭合祭，迄無定論。」

translations.literal: Through Eastern Han to Song for more than a thousand years, separate sacrifice and joint sacrifice—to the end there was no settled conclusion."
translations.idiomatic: For more than a thousand years from Eastern Han through Song, separate and joint sacrifice were debated without ever reaching a settled conclusion."

sentences.zh: 集議曰：「《周禮》，冬至圜丘禮天，夏至方丘禮地，時既不同，禮樂亦異。

translations.literal: Collective deliberation said: "In the Rites of Zhou, at winter solstice the round mound rites heaven, at summer solstice the square mound rites earth; the seasons being different, ritual and music are also different.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly resolved: "The Rites of Zhou prescribe rites to heaven at the round mound at winter solstice and rites to earth at the square mound at summer solstice. The seasons differ, and so do ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 王莽之制，何可法也。

translations.literal: Wang Mang's institutions—how can they be taken as model?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Wang Mang's institutions be taken as a model?

sentences.zh: 今當循唐、虞、三代之典，惟祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Now we should follow the canons of Tang of Yu, Shun, and the Three Dynasties, sacrificing only to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We should now follow the canon of Tang, Yu, Shun, and the Three Dynasties and sacrifice only to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其方丘祭地之禮，續議以聞。」

translations.literal: The square mound rite of sacrificing to earth—further deliberation will be reported."
translations.idiomatic: The square mound rite for sacrificing to earth should be deliberated further and reported."

sentences.zh: 按《周禮》，壇壝三成，近代增外四成，以廣天文從祀之位。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, the altar mound has three tiers; in recent times an outer fourth tier was added to broaden positions for astronomical attendant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites of Zhou the altar mound has three tiers; in recent times a fourth outer tier was added to make room for attendant spirits in the astronomical cult.

sentences.zh: 集議曰：「依《周禮》三成之制。

translations.literal: Collective deliberation said: "Follow the Rites of Zhou's three-tier system.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly resolved: "Follow the three-tier system of the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 然《周禮》疏雲每成一尺，不見縱廣之度。

translations.literal: Yet the commentary on the Rites of Zhou says each tier is one chi in height, without dimensions for length and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the commentary on the Rites of Zhou gives each tier as one chi in height and says nothing about length and breadth.

sentences.zh: 恐壇上狹隘，器物難容，擬四成制內減去一成，以合陽奇之數。

translations.literal: Fearing the altar top would be cramped and vessels hard to accommodate, we propose within the four-tier system to reduce by one tier, to accord with the yang odd number.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the altar summit would be too cramped for the vessels, we propose reducing the four-tier design by one tier to accord with the yang odd number.

sentences.zh: 每成高八尺一寸，以合乾之九九。

translations.literal: Each tier eight chi one cun in height, to accord with Qian's nine nines.
translations.idiomatic: Each tier should be eight chi and one cun high, matching the nine nines of Qian.

sentences.zh: 上成縱廣五丈，中成十丈，下成十五丈。

translations.literal: Upper tier five zhang in length and breadth, middle tier ten zhang, lower tier fifteen zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier five zhang square, the middle ten zhang, the lower fifteen zhang.

sentences.zh: 四陛，陛十有二級。

translations.literal: Four stairways, each stairway twelve steps.
translations.idiomatic: Four stairways, each with twelve steps.

sentences.zh: 外設二壝，內壝去壇二十五步，外壝去內壝五十四步，壝各四門。

translations.literal: Outside set two enclosures; inner enclosure twenty-five paces from the altar, outer enclosure fifty-four paces from the inner enclosure; each enclosure has four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Two enclosures were set outside: the inner twenty-five paces from the altar, the outer fifty-four paces from the inner; each enclosure had four gates.

sentences.zh: 壇設於丙巳之地，以就陽位」按古者，親祀冕無旒，服大裘而加袞。

translations.literal: The altar set in the bing-si direction, to take the yang position." According to antiquity, for personal sacrifice the cap had no tassels, wearing great fur robe with dragon robe added.
translations.idiomatic: The altar should stand in the bing-si direction to take the yang position." In antiquity the officiant wore a tasselless cap, a great fur robe, and a dragon robe over it.

sentences.zh: 臣下從祀，冠服歷代所尚，其制不同。

translations.literal: For ministers attending sacrifice, caps and robes esteemed by each dynasty—their systems differ.
translations.idiomatic: The caps and robes of ministers attending sacrifice differed in what each dynasty esteemed.

sentences.zh: 集議曰：「依宗廟見用冠服制度。」

translations.literal: Collective deliberation said: "Follow the cap and robe system currently used at the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly resolved: "Follow the cap and robe system now used at the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 按《周禮·大司樂》云：「凡樂，圜鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太簇為征，姑洗為羽，雷鼓雷鼗，孤竹之管，雲和之琴瑟，雲門之舞，冬至日於地上之圜丘奏之。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, Grand Master of Music: "For all music, round bell as gong, yellow bell as jue, taicu as zhi, guxian as yu, thunder drums and thunder tambourines, lone bamboo pipes, Yunhe zithers, Yun Gate dance—on winter solstice day perform it at the round mound on earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Grand Master of Music, says: "In all music the round bell serves as gong, the yellow bell as jue, taicu as zhi, guxian as yu; with thunder drums and tambourines, lone bamboo pipes, Yunhe zithers, and the Yun Gate dance—it is performed at the round mound on earth on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 若樂六變，則天神皆降，可得而禮矣。」

translations.literal: If the music undergoes six changes, then heavenly spirits all descend and can be received in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When the music undergoes six changes, the heavenly spirits all descend and may be received in ritual."

sentences.zh: 集議曰：「樂者所以動天地，感鬼神，必訪求深知音律之人，審五聲八音，以司肄樂。」

translations.literal: Collective deliberation said: "Music is that whereby heaven and earth are moved and ghosts and spirits are touched; one must seek out persons deeply versed in pitch and law, examine the five tones and eight sounds, to oversee practice of music."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly resolved: "Music moves heaven and earth and touches ghosts and spirits. We must seek out those deeply versed in pitch and law, examine the five tones and eight sounds, and put them in charge of musical practice."

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬辰，中書復集議。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month renchen—the Secretariat again held collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day in the fourth month of summer the Secretariat convened again for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 博士言：「舊制神位版用木。」

translations.literal: An erudite said: "By old regulation spirit tablets used wood."
translations.idiomatic: An erudite said: "Under the old regulation spirit tablets were made of wood."

sentences.zh: 中書議，改用蒼玉金字，白玉為座。

translations.literal: The Secretariat deliberated to change to dark jade with gold characters, white jade as base.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat proposed instead dark jade with gold characters on a white jade base.

sentences.zh: 博士曰：「郊祀尚質，合依舊制。」

translations.literal: The erudite said: "Suburban sacrifice esteems simplicity; it is fitting to follow the old regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The erudite replied: "Suburban sacrifice esteems simplicity; we should follow the old regulation."

sentences.zh: 遂用木主，長二尺五寸，闊一尺二寸，上圓下方，丹漆金字，木用松柏，貯以紅漆匣，黃羅帕覆之。

translations.literal: Thereupon wooden spirit tablets were used, two chi five cun long, one chi two cun wide, round above and square below, vermilion lacquer with gold characters, wood of pine and cypress, stored in a red lacquer case, covered with yellow silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden spirit tablets were therefore used: two chi five cun long and one chi two cun wide, round above and square below, vermilion lacquer with gold characters, pine or cypress wood, kept in a red lacquer case and covered with yellow silk.

sentences.zh: 造畢，有司議所以藏。

translations.literal: When manufacture was complete, the relevant offices deliberated where to store them.
translations.idiomatic: When they were finished, the relevant offices debated where to store them.

sentences.zh: 議者復謂，神主廟則有之，今祀於壇，對越在上，非若他神無所見也。

translations.literal: Deliberators again said: spirit tablets exist for temples; now sacrificing at the altar, facing and responding above, it is not like other spirits with nothing visible.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators argued again that spirit tablets belong in temples; here sacrifice is on the altar, face to face above—not like other spirits who have no visible presence.

sentences.zh: 所制神主遂不用。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets that had been made were therefore not used.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets that had been made were therefore not used.

sentences.zh: 七月九日，博士又言：「古者祀天，器用陶匏，席用槁鞂。

translations.literal: Ninth day, seventh month—the erudite again said: "In antiquity sacrificing to heaven, vessels used pottery and gourds, mats used straw and reeds.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the seventh month the erudite said again: "In antiquity sacrifice to heaven used pottery and gourd vessels and straw and reed mats.

sentences.zh: 自漢甘泉雍畤之祀，以迄後漢、魏、晉、南北二朝、隋、唐，其壇壝玉帛禮器儀仗，日益繁縟，浸失古者尚質之意。

translations.literal: From Han's Ganquan and Yongzhi sacrifices through Later Han, Wei, Jin, Northern and Southern Dynasties, Sui, and Tang, their altar mounds, jade and silk, ritual vessels, and ceremonial regalia grew daily more elaborate, gradually losing antiquity's intent of esteeming simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ganquan and Yongzhi sacrifices of Han through Later Han, Wei, Jin, the Northern and Southern Dynasties, Sui, and Tang, altar mounds, jade and silk, ritual vessels, and ceremonial regalia grew ever more elaborate, gradually losing antiquity's esteem for simplicity.

sentences.zh: 宋、金多循唐制，其壇壝禮器，考之於經，固未能全合，其儀法具在。

translations.literal: Song and Jin mostly followed Tang institutions; their altar mounds and ritual vessels, examined against the classics, indeed could not fully accord, yet their ceremonial regulations are fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Jin mostly followed Tang practice; their altars and ritual vessels, checked against the classics, could not fully conform, yet their ceremonial regulations survive intact.

sentences.zh: 當時名儒輩出，亦未嘗不援經而定也，酌古今以行禮，亦宜焉。

translations.literal: At the time famous Confucians emerged in succession; they too never failed to cite the classics in fixing rites; weighing antiquity and present to conduct ritual is also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Famous scholars of the time likewise appealed to the classics in fixing ritual; weighing past and present to conduct sacrifice is also fitting.

sentences.zh: 今檢討唐、宋、金親祀、攝行儀註，並雅樂節次，合從集議。」

translations.literal: Now examine Tang, Song, and Jin regulations for personal sacrifice and proxy performance, together with elegant music sequences—all should follow collective deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: We should now review Tang, Song, and Jin regulations for personal and proxy sacrifice, together with the sequences of elegant music, and follow the collective deliberation."

sentences.zh: 太常議曰：「郊祀之事，聖朝自平定金、宋以來，未暇舉行，今欲修嚴，不能一舉而大備。

translations.literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies deliberated: "Matters of suburban sacrifice—the sage dynasty since pacifying Jin and Song has had no leisure to perform them; now wishing to restore strict observance, one cannot in a single effort achieve full preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies replied: "Suburban sacrifice has not been performed since the dynasty pacified Jin and Song; if we now wish to restore it strictly, we cannot prepare everything at once.

sentences.zh: 然始議之際，亦須酌古今之儀，垂則後來。

translations.literal: Yet at the beginning of deliberation, one must also weigh antiquity and present in ritual, leaving a standard for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even at the outset we must weigh past and present ritual and leave a standard for later generations.

sentences.zh: 請從中書會翰林、集賢、禮官及明禮之士，講明去取以聞。」

translations.literal: We request that the Secretariat convene Hanlin, Academy of Scholarly Worthies, rites officials, and persons versed in ritual, to clarify what to adopt and reject and report."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Secretariat convene the Hanlin Academy, the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, rites officials, and scholars versed in ritual to clarify what to adopt and reject and report back."

sentences.zh: 中書集議曰：「合行禮儀，非草創所能備。

translations.literal: The Secretariat's collective deliberation said: "The ritual to be performed cannot be fully prepared by improvisation alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat resolved: "The full ritual cannot be prepared from scratch in a single effort.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋皆有攝行之禮，除從祀受胙外，一切儀註，悉依唐制修之。」

translations.literal: Tang and Song both had rites for acting in proxy; apart from secondary worship and receiving sacrificial portions, all ritual regulations shall be revised entirely according to Tang practice."
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Song both knew rites performed by proxy. Except for secondary worship and the sharing of sacrificial meat, every detail of the regulations should be drawn up again along Tang lines."

sentences.zh: 八月十二日，太常寺言：「尊祖配天，其禮儀樂章別有常典，若俟至日議之，恐匆遽有誤。」

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the eighth month, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "Honoring the ancestors alongside Heaven has its own established ritual and music; if we wait until the solstice day to deliberate, we fear haste may lead to error."
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth of the eighth month the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "To honor the ancestors beside Heaven has fixed rites and hymns of its own. If we leave discussion until the solstice, we may blunder in the rush."

sentences.zh: 於是中書省臣奏曰：「自古漢人有天下，其祖宗皆配天享祭，臣等與平章何榮祖議，宗廟已依時祭享，今郊祀止祭天。」

translations.literal: Thereupon ministers of the Central Secretariat memorialized: "Since ancient times, when Han people have held the realm, their ancestors have all been associated with Heaven in sacrifice. We, together with Counselor He Rongzu, have discussed this: the ancestral temple already receives seasonal offerings; at the suburban sacrifice we now worship Heaven alone."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat then submitted: "From antiquity, whenever Han Chinese ruled the world, their forebears were joined to Heaven in sacrifice. We have consulted with Counselor He Rongzu. The ancestral temple already receives its seasonal rites; at the suburban altar we propose to worship Heaven only."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "Let it be so."

sentences.zh: 是歲南郊，配位遂省。

translations.literal: That year at the southern suburb, the associated seat was accordingly omitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year at the southern suburb, the seat of the associate was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十一年，武宗即位。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Emperor Wuzong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲子，命御史大夫鐵古叠兒即南郊告謝天地，主用柏素，質玄書，為即位告謝之始。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on day jiazi, he ordered Grand Censor Tiegu Die'er to proceed at once to the southern suburb to report and give thanks to Heaven and Earth; the principal offerings used plain cypress, with black-ground documents—marking the beginning of accession thanksgiving.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day in the seventh month of autumn he sent Grand Censor Tiegu Die'er straight to the southern suburb to announce his accession and thank Heaven and Earth. Plain cypress was the chief offering; the memorials were written on black-ground paper. Thus began the rite of thanksgiving at enthronement.

sentences.zh: 至大二年冬十月乙酉，尚書省臣及太常禮官言：「郊祀者國之大禮，今南郊之禮已行而未備，北郊之禮尚未舉行。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, year 2 of Zhida, on day yiyou, ministers of the Secretariat and ritual officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "Suburban sacrifice is the great rite of the state. The southern suburb rite has been performed but is not yet complete, and the northern suburb rite has not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the tenth month of winter, the second year of Zhida, Secretariat ministers and ritual officers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: "Suburban sacrifice is the greatest ceremony of the realm. The southern rite has been held but remains incomplete; the northern rite has not yet been performed at all.

sentences.zh: 今年冬至南郊，請以太祖聖武皇帝配享；

translations.literal: At the southern suburb this winter solstice, we request that the founding emperor Taizu Shengwu be associated in the offering;
translations.idiomatic: At this winter solstice at the southern suburb, let Founder Taizu Shengwu share the offering;

sentences.zh: 明年夏至北郊，以世祖皇帝配。」

translations.literal: Next year at summer solstice at the northern suburb, let Emperor Shizu be associated."
translations.idiomatic: Next summer solstice at the northern suburb, let Emperor Shizu be associated."

sentences.zh: 帝皆是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented to every point.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲辰朔，尚書太尉右丞相、太保左丞相、田司徒、郝參政等復奏曰：「南郊祭天於圜丘，大禮已舉。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, jiachen, Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat and Right Chancellor, Grand Guardian and Left Chancellor, Situ Tian, Counsellor Hao, and others again memorialized: "Heaven was sacrificed to at the Round Mound in the southern suburb; the great ceremony has been performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, a jiachen day, the Secretariat Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor, the Grand Guardian and Left Chancellor, Situ Tian, Counsellor Hao, and others memorialized again: "Heaven has been worshipped at the Round Mound in the southern suburb; the great rite is done.

sentences.zh: 其北郊祭皇地祇於方澤，並神州地祇、五嶽四瀆、山林川澤及朝日夕月，此有國家所當崇禮者也。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Imperial Earth at the Square Pond in the northern suburb, together with the Earth of the Divine Land, the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Great Rivers, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes, and the Morning Sun and Evening Moon—these are what a state ought to honor with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Worship of Imperial Earth at the Square Pond in the north, together with the Earth of the Divine Land, the Five Peaks and Four Rivers, mountains and forests, rivers and marshes, and the Morning Sun and Evening Moon—these are rites a realm is bound to uphold.

sentences.zh: 當聖明御極而弗舉行，恐遂廢弛。」

translations.literal: Under sage illumination at the apex of rule not to carry them out—we fear they will fall into neglect."
translations.idiomatic: If, under a sage on the throne, we still do not perform them, we fear they will lapse entirely."

sentences.zh: 制若曰：「卿議甚是，其即行焉。」

translations.literal: The edict ran: "Your deliberation is most apt; carry it out at once."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Your proposal is sound. Execute it without delay."

sentences.zh: 至大三年春正月，中書禮部移太常禮儀院，下博士擬定北郊從祀、朝日夕月禮儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring, year 3 of Zhida, the Rites Office of the Central Secretariat forwarded to the Court of Ritual Protocol, ordering the erudites to draft the northern suburb secondary sacrifices and the rites of the Morning Sun and Evening Moon.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the third year of Zhida, the Secretariat Rites Office referred the matter to the Court of Ritual Protocol and charged the erudites with drafting the northern suburb secondary worship and the rites of the Morning Sun and Evening Moon.

sentences.zh: 博士李之紹、蔣汝礪疏曰：「按方丘之禮，夏以五月，商以六月，周以夏至，其丘在國之北。

translations.literal: Erudites Li Zhishao and Jiang Ruli memorialized: "According to the Square Mound rite: Xia in the fifth month, Shang in the sixth, Zhou at summer solstice; the mound lies north of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Li Zhishao and Jiang Ruli submitted: "The Square Mound rite: Xia performed it in the fifth month, Shang in the sixth, Zhou at summer solstice. The mound stood north of the capital.

sentences.zh: 禮神之玉以黃琮，牲用黃犢，幣用黃繒，配以後稷。

translations.literal: Jade for worshipping the spirit is the yellow ceremonial tube; victims are yellow calves; silks are yellow; Hou Ji is associated.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow jade tube honored the spirit; offerings were yellow calves and yellow silk; Hou Ji stood as associate.

sentences.zh: 其方壇之制，漢去都城四里，為壇四陛。

translations.literal: For the square altar: Han placed it four li from the capital, with four flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: As for the square altar: the Han set it four li from the capital, with four flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 唐去宮城北十四里，為方壇八角三成，每成高四尺，上闊十六步，設陛。

translations.literal: Tang placed it fourteen li north of the palace city, an octagonal square altar of three tiers, each tier four feet high, the top sixteen paces wide, with steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang set it fourteen li north of the palace city: an octagonal altar in three tiers, each four feet high, the upper platform sixteen paces across, with steps on every side.

sentences.zh: 上等陛廣八尺，中等陛一丈，下等陛廣一丈二尺。

translations.literal: The upper steps were eight feet wide, the middle ten feet, the lower twelve feet wide.
translations.idiomatic: The upper flight was eight feet wide, the middle ten, the lower twelve.

sentences.zh: 宋至徽宗始定為再成。

translations.literal: Under Song, only from Emperor Huizong onward was it fixed at two tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, only from Emperor Huizong on was it reduced to two tiers.

sentences.zh: 歷代制雖不同，然無出於三成之式。

translations.literal: Regulations differed through the ages, yet none departed from the three-tier pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty shaped the rite differently, yet none escaped the pattern of three tiers.

sentences.zh: 今擬取坤數用六之義，去都城北六里，於壬地選擇善地，於中為方壇，三成四陛，外為三壝。

translations.literal: We now propose taking the K'un number and the meaning of six: six li north of the capital, selecting good ground in the ren direction, establishing a square altar at the center, three tiers and four flights, with three enclosures outside.
translations.idiomatic: We propose to follow the K'un number and the virtue of six: six li north of the capital, a favorable site in the ren quarter, a square altar at the center in three tiers with four flights, and three enclosures beyond.

sentences.zh: 仍依古制，自外壝之外，治四面稍令低下，以應澤中之制。

translations.literal: Still following ancient form, beyond the outer enclosure the four sides were to be leveled slightly lower, matching the regulation of the pond-center.
translations.idiomatic: As in antiquity, outside the outermost enclosure the ground on all four sides should slope gently downward, in keeping with the rite performed in the heart of the marsh.

sentences.zh: 宮室、墻圍、器皿色，並用黃。

translations.literal: Palace chambers, walls, vessels, and colors—all were to use yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Halls, walls, vessels, and colors should all be yellow.

sentences.zh: 其再成八角八陛，非古制，難用。

translations.literal: The two-tier octagon with eight flights is not ancient form and is difficult to employ.
translations.idiomatic: The two-tier octagon with eight flights is not the ancient pattern and should not be used.

sentences.zh: 其神州地祇以下從祀，自漢以來，歷代制度不一，至唐始因隋制，以嶽鎮海瀆、山林川澤、丘陵墳衍原隰，各從其方從祀。

translations.literal: Secondary sacrifice below the Earth of the Divine Land: since Han, systems differed; Tang first followed Sui, with peaks, towns, seas, rivers, mountains, forests, marshes, mounds, tombs, plains, marshes, heights, and lowlands—each sacrificed from its direction.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary worship below the Earth of the Divine Land: since Han the arrangements have varied. Tang first adopted Sui practice, placing the sacred peaks, coastal shrines, rivers, mountains, forests, marshes, mounds, tombs, open plains, wetlands, heights, and lowlands each in its proper quarter as attendant spirits.

sentences.zh: 今盍參酌舉行。」

translations.literal: Now let us consult and carry them out."
translations.idiomatic: Let us weigh these precedents and put the rite in motion."

sentences.zh: 秋九月，太常禮儀院復下博士，檢討合用器物。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, the Court of Ritual Protocol again ordered the erudites to examine and confirm the requisite implements.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Court of Ritual Protocol again charged the erudites to review the vessels and regalia required.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙申，有事於南郊，以太祖配，五方帝日月星辰從祀。

translations.literal: On day bingshen in the eleventh month, the southern suburb ceremony was held; Taizu was associated; the Five Directional Emperors, sun, moon, and stars were secondary.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day in the eleventh month the southern suburb rite was performed. Taizu shared the offering; the Five Emperors of the directions, the sun, moon, and stars attended as secondary spirits.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐元年夏四月丁亥，太常寺臣請立北郊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, year 1 of Yanyou of Emperor Renzong, day dinghai, officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested establishment of the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, the first year of Yanyou under Emperor Renzong, on dinghai day, officers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices asked that the northern suburb be established.

sentences.zh: 帝謙遜未遑，北郊之議遂輟。

translations.literal: The emperor in modesty had no leisure; discussion of the northern suburb ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, deferring in humility, had not the leisure; the northern suburb proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 英宗至治二年九月，有旨議南郊祀事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, year 2 of Zhizhi of Emperor Yingzong, an edict ordered discussion of southern suburb sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Zhizhi, Emperor Yingzong commanded deliberation on the southern suburb sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 中書平章買閭，御史中丞曹立，禮部尚書張野，學士蔡文淵、袁桷、鄧文原，太常禮儀院使王緯、田天澤，博士劉致等會都堂議：

translations.literal: Counselor-in-chief Mai Lu, Vice Censor-in-chief Cao Li, Minister of Rites Zhang Ye, academicians Cai Wenyuan, Yuan Que, and Deng Wenyuan, directors of the Court of Ritual Protocol Wang Wei and Tian Tianze, erudite Liu Zhi, and others met at the capital hall to deliberate:
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Mai Lu, Vice Censor-in-chief Cao Li, Minister of Rites Zhang Ye, Hanlin academicians Cai Wenyuan, Yuan Que, and Deng Wenyuan, directors of the Court of Ritual Protocol Wang Wei and Tian Tianze, erudite Liu Zhi, and others assembled in the capital hall to deliberate:

sentences.zh: 一曰年分，按前代多三年一祀，天子即位已及三年，常有旨欽依。

translations.literal: First: interval of years. Previous ages mostly sacrificed once every three years; once three years have passed since the Son of Heaven took the throne, edicts commonly follow this.
translations.idiomatic: First, the cycle of years. Earlier dynasties usually sacrificed once every three years; when three years had passed since the Son of Heaven took the throne, an edict normally confirmed the practice.

sentences.zh: 二曰神位。

translations.literal: Second: spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the seats of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·大宗伯》，「以禋祀祀昊天上帝」。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward: "with smoke sacrifice worship Haotian Shangdi."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Grand Steward of Rites: "With the smoke sacrifice one worships Haotian Shangdi."

sentences.zh: 註謂：「昊天上帝，冬至圜丘所祀天皇大帝也。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: "Haotian Shangdi is the Great Heavenly Emperor worshipped at the Round Mound at winter solstice."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains: "Haotian Shangdi is the Great Heavenly Emperor honored at the Round Mound on the winter solstice."

sentences.zh: 又曰「蒼璧禮天」。

translations.literal: It also says, "with the green disk sacrifice to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "With the green jade disk one sacrifices to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 註云：「此禮天以冬至，謂天皇大帝也。

translations.literal: The commentary states: "This sacrifice to Heaven at winter solstice refers to the Great Heavenly Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Another note reads: "This winter-solstice worship of Heaven means the Great Heavenly Emperor.

sentences.zh: 在北極，謂之北辰。」

translations.literal: At the North Pole, called the North Star."
translations.idiomatic: He dwells at the North Pole and is called the North Star."

sentences.zh: 又云：「北辰天皇耀魄寶也，又名昊天上帝，又名太一帝君，以其尊大，故有數名。」

translations.literal: It also states: "The North Star is the Heavenly Emperor Yaopobao; also called Haotian Shangdi, also called the Great Unity Lord; so august that it has several names."
translations.idiomatic: It adds: "The North Star is the Heavenly Emperor Yaopobao, also named Haotian Shangdi, also named the Lord of Great Unity—so exalted that it bears many titles."

sentences.zh: 今按《晉書·天文志·中宮》「鉤陳口中一星曰天皇大帝，其神耀魄寶」。

translations.literal: Now according to the Jin History, Treatise on Astronomy, Central Palace: "One star at the mouth of Gouchen is called the Great Heavenly Emperor; its spirit is Yaopobao."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin History, Treatise on Astronomy, Central Palace, records: "A single star at the mouth of Gouchen is the Great Heavenly Emperor; its spirit is Yaopobao."

sentences.zh: 《周禮》所祀天神，正言昊天上帝。

translations.literal: The heavenly spirit that the Rites of Zhou sacrifices to is properly called Haotian Shangdi.
translations.idiomatic: The celestial spirit named in the Rites of Zhou is precisely Haotian Shangdi.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏以星經推之，乃謂即天皇大帝。

translations.literal: Master Zheng, deducing from the star canon, thus identified it with the Great Heavenly Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zheng, reasoning from the star classic, identified this spirit with the Great Heavenly Emperor.

sentences.zh: 然漢、魏以來，名號亦復不一。

translations.literal: Yet from Han and Wei onward, titles were likewise not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Han and Wei on, the names were never settled.

sentences.zh: 漢初曰上帝，曰太一，曰皇天上帝。

translations.literal: Early Han called it Shangdi, Taiyi, and Huangtian Shangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han spoke of Shangdi, of Taiyi, of Huangtian Shangdi.

sentences.zh: 魏曰皇皇帝天。

translations.literal: Wei called it Huanghuangdi Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei called it Huanghuangdi Tian.

sentences.zh: 梁曰天皇大帝。

translations.literal: Liang called it the Great Heavenly Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang called it the Great Heavenly Emperor.

sentences.zh: 惟西晉曰昊天上帝，與《周禮》合。

translations.literal: Only Western Jin said Haotian Shangdi, matching the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only Western Jin used Haotian Shangdi, in accord with the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋以來，壇上既設昊天上帝，第一等復有天皇大帝，其五天帝與太一、天一等，皆不經見。

translations.literal: From Tang and Song, on the altar Haotian Shangdi was already set; the first rank again had the Great Heavenly Emperor; the Five Heavenly Emperors with Taiyi, Tianyi, and such—all lack canonical warrant.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang and Song onward the altar already bore Haotian Shangdi, yet the first rank also included the Great Heavenly Emperor; the Five Heavenly Emperors, Taiyi, Tianyi, and the like appear nowhere in the classics.

sentences.zh: 本朝大德九年，中書圓議，止依《周禮》，祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Our dynasty in year 9 of Dade, the Central Secretariat's round deliberation, following only the Rites of Zhou, sacrificed to Haotian Shangdi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dade our dynasty, after round deliberation in the Central Secretariat, worshipped only Haotian Shangdi, as the Rites of Zhou prescribe.

sentences.zh: 至大三年圓議，五帝從享，依前代通祭。

translations.literal: In year 3 of Zhida round deliberation, the Five Emperors shared the offering, following previous ages' universal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhida, round deliberation allowed the Five Emperors to share the offering, following the comprehensive sacrifice of earlier times.

sentences.zh: 三曰配位。

translations.literal: Third: associated seats.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the seats of associates.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》曰：「孝莫大於嚴父，嚴父莫大於配天。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Of filial piety none is greater than honoring the father; of honoring the father none is greater than associating him with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "No filial act surpasses honoring the father; no honor to the father surpasses joining him to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「郊祀后稷以配天。」

translations.literal: It also says: "At suburban sacrifice Hou Ji is associated to match Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "At the suburban rite Hou Ji is joined to Heaven as associate."

sentences.zh: 此郊之所以有配也。

translations.literal: This is why suburban sacrifice has an associate.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the suburban altar always has an associate.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐已下，莫不皆然。

translations.literal: From Han and Tang downward, none was otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Tang down, none did otherwise.

sentences.zh: 至大三年冬十月三日，奉旨十一月冬至合祭南郊，太祖皇帝配，圓議取旨。

translations.literal: On the third day of the tenth month of winter, year 3 of Zhida, by edict the joint southern suburb sacrifice at winter solstice in the eleventh month would have Founder Taizu associated; round deliberation awaits decree.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the tenth month of winter in the third year of Zhida, by edict the southern suburb sacrifice at the winter solstice in the eleventh month would have Founder Taizu as associate; round deliberation awaits the throne's word.

sentences.zh: 四曰告配。

translations.literal: Fourth: announcement of the associate.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, announcing the associate.

sentences.zh: 《禮器》曰：「魯人將有事於上帝，必先有事於頖宮。」

translations.literal: Ritual Implements says: "When the people of Lu were about to sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, they must first sacrifice at the palace school."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Implements says: "When the men of Lu were to worship the Supreme Lord, they first had business at the palace school."

sentences.zh: 註：「告後稷也，告之者，將以配天也。」

translations.literal: Commentary: "announcing to Hou Ji; the announcer will associate him with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary: "This is to announce to Hou Ji—for the one announced will stand beside Heaven."

sentences.zh: 告用牛一。

translations.literal: Announcement uses one ox."
translations.idiomatic: The announcement requires one ox.

sentences.zh: 《宋會要》於致齋二日，宿廟告配，凡遣官犧尊豆籩，行一獻禮。

translations.literal: Song Essential Documents: on the second day of austere preparation, lodging in the temple to announce the associate; officials dispatched with sacrificial vessels, performing one presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Essential Documents: on the second day of the austere fast, officials lodged in the temple to announce the associate, sending officers with sacrificial vessels to perform a single presentation.

sentences.zh: 至大三年十一月二十一日，質明行事。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, year 3 of Zhida, at dawn the rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month in the third year of Zhida, at daybreak the ceremony was carried out.

sentences.zh: 初獻攝太尉同太常禮儀院官赴太廟奏告，圓議取旨。

translations.literal: The first presenter, acting Grand Preceptor, together with Court of Ritual Protocol officials went to the ancestral temple to report; round deliberation awaits decree.
translations.idiomatic: The first presenter, the Grand Preceptor by proxy, with officers of the Court of Ritual Protocol, would go to the ancestral temple to announce the rite; round deliberation awaits decree.

sentences.zh: 五曰大裘冕。

translations.literal: Fifth: great fur robe and cap.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the great fur robe and cap.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》司裘「掌為大裘，以共王祀天之服」，鄭司農雲，黑羊裘，服以祀天，示質也。

translations.literal: Rites of Zhou, Master of Furs: "in charge of the great fur robe for the king's robes when sacrificing to Heaven"; Zheng the Former Farmer said, black sheep fur robe, worn to sacrifice to Heaven, showing simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Master of Furs: "He prepares the great fur robe for the king's service when sacrificing to Heaven." Zheng the Former Farmer explained: a robe of black sheepskin, worn to worship Heaven, to show plainness.

sentences.zh: 弁師「掌王之五冕」，註：「冕服有六，而言五者，大裘之冕蓋無旒，不聯數也。」

translations.literal: Cap-maker: "in charge of the king's five caps"; commentary: "cap-robes are six, yet five are spoken because the great fur robe cap likely has no tassels and is not counted in the series."
translations.idiomatic: The Cap-maker: "He keeps the king's five caps." The note says: "There are six cap-robes, yet only five are named because the cap of the great fur robe has no tassels and is not reckoned in the count."

sentences.zh: 《禮記·郊特牲》曰：「郊之祭也，迎長日之至也。

translations.literal: Record of Rites, Suburban Special Victims: "The suburban sacrifice welcomes the arrival of the lengthening day.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites, Suburban Special Victims: "The suburban rite greets the coming of the longer day.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，王被袞以象天，戴冕璪十有二旒，則天數也。」

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, the king wears the dragon robe to symbolize Heaven, wears the cap with twelve beads—that is Heaven's number."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice the king dons the dragon robe in image of Heaven and the cap with twelve beads—that is Heaven's number."

sentences.zh: 陸佃曰：「禮不盛服不充，蓋服大裘以袞襲之也。

translations.literal: Lu Dian said: "Rites do not allow insufficient dress to suffice; likely wear the great fur robe with the dragon robe over it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dian said: "Rites forbid offering less than full dress; presumably one wears the great fur robe beneath the dragon robe.

sentences.zh: 謂冬至服大裘，被之以袞。

translations.literal: Meaning: at winter solstice wear the great fur robe, covered with the dragon robe.
translations.idiomatic: That is: at the winter solstice one wears the great fur robe and covers it with the dragon robe.

sentences.zh: 開元及開寶《通禮》，鸞駕出宮，服袞冕至大次，質明改服大裘冕而出次。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan and Kaibao Comprehensive Rites: imperial carriage leaves palace in dragon robe and cap to the great tent; at dawn change to great fur robe and cap and leave the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan and Kaibao Comprehensive Rites: the imperial procession leaves the palace in dragon robe and cap and halts at the great tent; at dawn the king changes into the great fur robe and cap and steps from the tent.

sentences.zh: 《宋會要》紹興十三年，車駕自廟赴青城，服通天冠、絳紗袍，祀日服大裘袞冕。

translations.literal: Song Essential Documents, year 13 of Shaoxing: carriage from temple to Azure City in communication-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe; on sacrifice day wear great fur robe and dragon cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Essential Documents, thirteenth year of Shaoxing: from the temple to the Azure City the emperor wore the communication-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe; on the day of sacrifice he wore the great fur robe and dragon cap.

sentences.zh: 圓議用袞冕，取旨。

translations.literal: Round deliberation: use dragon robe and cap, await decree.
translations.idiomatic: Round deliberation proposed the dragon robe and cap; the matter awaits decree.

sentences.zh: 六曰匏爵。

translations.literal: Sixth: gourd goblets.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the gourd goblets.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》曰：「郊之祭也，器用陶匏，以象天地之性也。」

translations.literal: Suburban Special Victims: "At suburban sacrifice, vessels are pottery and gourd, to image the nature of Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Suburban Special Victims: "At the suburban rite the vessels are pottery and gourd, imaging the nature of Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 註謂：「陶瓦器，匏用酌獻酒。」

translations.literal: Commentary: "pottery earthenware; gourd used to pour presentation wine."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary: "Pottery for earthen vessels; gourd for pouring the wine of presentation."

sentences.zh: 《開元禮》、《開寶禮》皆有匏爵。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan Rites and Kaibao Rites both have gourd goblets.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Kaiyuan Rites and the Kaibao Rites prescribe gourd goblets.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，正配位用匏爵有坫。

translations.literal: Year 9 of Dade, principal and associated seats used gourd goblets with stands.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dade the principal and associate seats used gourd goblets on stands.

sentences.zh: 圓議正位用匏，配位飲福用玉爵，取旨。

translations.literal: Round deliberation: principal seat uses gourd; associated seat for drinking blessing uses jade goblet, await decree.
translations.idiomatic: Round deliberation: the principal seat would use gourd; the associate would drink the blessing wine from a jade goblet—the matter awaits decree.

sentences.zh: 七曰戒誓。

translations.literal: Seventh: admonition and oath.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the admonition and oath.

sentences.zh: 唐《通典》引《禮經》，祭前期十日親戒百官及族人，太宰總戒群官。

translations.literal: Tang Comprehensive Institutions cites the Rites Classic: ten days before sacrifice the ruler personally admonishes the hundred officials and clansmen; the Grand Steward issues general admonition to all officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Comprehensive Institutions quotes the Rites Classic: ten days before the sacrifice the ruler admonishes the hundred officials and his kin in person; the Grand Steward issues a general admonition to the whole bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 唐前祀七日，《宋會要》十日。

translations.literal: Tang seven days before sacrifice; Song Essential Documents ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Tang practice allowed seven days; the Song Essential Documents prescribe ten.

sentences.zh: 《纂要》太尉南向，司徒、亞終獻、一品、二品從祀北向，行事官以次北向，禮直官以誓文授之太尉讀。

translations.literal: Compendium Essentials: Grand Preceptor faces south; Minister of Education, secondary and final presenters, first and second ranks of secondary sacrifice face north; officiants in order face north; ritual supervisor hands the oath text to the Grand Preceptor to read.
translations.idiomatic: The Compendium Essentials: the Grand Preceptor faces south; the Minister of Education, the secondary and final presenters, and the first- and second-rank associates face north; officiants stand northward in order; the ritual supervisor hands the oath to the Grand Preceptor to read aloud.

sentences.zh: 今天子親行大禮，止令禮直局管勾讀誓文。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven personally performs the great rite; only the ritual supervisor's office is ordered to read the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Son of Heaven performs the great rite in person, only the ritual supervisor's office is charged with reading the oath.

sentences.zh: 圓議令管勾代太尉讀誓，刑部尚書蒞之。

translations.literal: Round deliberation: let the supervisor read the oath in place of the Grand Preceptor, with the Minister of Punishments presiding.
translations.idiomatic: Round deliberation proposed that the supervisor read the oath for the Grand Preceptor, under the oversight of the Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 八曰散齋、致齋。

translations.literal: Eighth: dispersal fast and austere fast.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the dispersal fast and the austere fast.

sentences.zh: 《禮經》前期十日，唐、宋、金皆七日，散齋四日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: Rites Classic ten days beforehand; Tang, Song, Jin all seven days; dispersal fast four days, austere fast three days.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Classic allow ten days; Tang, Song, and Jin all used seven—four days of dispersal fast and three of austere fast.

sentences.zh: 國朝親祀太廟七日，散齋四日於別殿，致齋三日於大明殿。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's personal sacrifice at the ancestral temple: seven days; dispersal fast four days in a separate hall; austere fast three days in the Great Brightness Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When our dynasty worships the ancestral temple in person, the term is seven days: four days of dispersal fast in a separate hall, three days of austere fast in the Hall of Great Brightness.

sentences.zh: 圓議依前七日。

translations.literal: The collegiate deliberation followed the previous seven days.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat’s roundtable decision kept the earlier seven-day rule.

sentences.zh: 十曰犧牲。

translations.literal: Tenth: sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth topic is sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 《郊特牲》曰：「郊特牲而社稷太牢。」

translations.literal: The Jiao Te Sheng says: “For suburban sacrifice use a special victim; for the altars of soil and grain use the grand complement.”
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Suburban Sacrifice says: “The suburban rite employs a special victim; the altars of soil and grain receive the full complement of ox, sheep, and pig.”

sentences.zh: 又曰：「天地之牛角繭栗。」

translations.literal: It also says: “For Heaven and Earth, the horns of the ox should be like cocoon and chestnut.”
translations.idiomatic: It adds: “Oxen offered to Heaven and Earth should have horns no larger than cocoon and chestnut buds.”

sentences.zh: 秦用騮駒。

translations.literal: Qin used bay colts.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin used bay colts.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝五帝共一牲，武帝三年一祀，用太牢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han used one victim for the Five Thearchs together; Emperor Wu sacrificed once every three years and used the grand complement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han offered a single victim to all five thearchs jointly; Emperor Wu held the rite every three years with the full ox-sheep-pig complement.

sentences.zh: 光武采元始故事，天地共犢。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu adopted the Yuan Shi precedent: Heaven and Earth shared one calf.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu followed the Yuan Shi precedent, using one calf for both Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 隋上帝、配帝，蒼犢二。

translations.literal: In Sui, for the Supreme Thearch and the associated thearch, two dark calves.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, the main and associated thearchs each received a dark calf—two in all.

sentences.zh: 唐開元用牛。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era of Tang, oxen were used.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Kaiyuan rite used oxen.

sentences.zh: 宋正位用蒼犢一，配位太牢一。

translations.literal: Song: for the principal seat one dark calf; for the associated seat one grand complement.
translations.idiomatic: In Song, the principal seat received one dark calf and the associated seat the full complement.

sentences.zh: 國朝大德九年，蒼犢二，羊豕各九。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, in the ninth year of Dade, two dark calves, and nine sheep and nine pigs each.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty’s ninth year of Dade, the offering comprised two dark calves plus nine sheep and nine pigs apiece.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，馬純色肥腯一，牲正副一，鹿一十八，野豬一十八，羊一十八，圓議依舊儀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida, one pure-colored plump horse; one principal and one secondary sacrificial victim; eighteen deer, eighteen wild boars, eighteen sheep—the collegiate deliberation followed the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 3 the list ran to one solid-colored fat horse, principal and secondary victims, and eighteen each of deer, wild boar, and sheep; the Secretariat deliberation held to the established rite.

sentences.zh: 神位配位用犢外，仍用馬，其餘並依舊日已行典禮。

translations.literal: Apart from calves for the divine and associated seats, horses were still used; all else followed the ceremonies already in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Calves served the main and associated divine seats, but horses were retained as well; everything else followed long-standing practice.

sentences.zh: 十一曰香鼎。

translations.literal: Eleventh: incense tripods.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh topic is incense censers.

sentences.zh: 大祭有三，始煙為歆神，始宗廟則焫蕭稞鬯，所謂臭陽達於墻屋者也。

translations.literal: Grand sacrifices have three kinds: first, smoke to delight the spirits; at the ancestral temple, burning artemisia with scented grain and libation—what is called letting the yang fragrance reach through the wall to the chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand sacrifices begin in three ways: with smoke to please the spirits; at the ancestral temple, by burning artemisia, scented grain, and libation—the “yang fragrance” said to penetrate the hall.

sentences.zh: 後世焚香，蓋本乎此，而非《禮經》之正。

translations.literal: Later ages’ burning of incense largely derives from this, yet it is not the orthodox form of the Rites Classic.
translations.idiomatic: Later ritual incense stems from this tradition, not from the canonical form in the Rites.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，用陶瓦香鼎五十，神座香鼎、香盒案各一。

translations.literal: In Zhida 3, fifty pottery incense tripods were used; one incense tripod and one incense-box stand for each spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhida 3 specified fifty earthenware censers, with one censer and one incense-tray stand at each spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 圓議依舊儀。

translations.literal: The collegiate deliberation followed the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat decision kept the old rite.

sentences.zh: 十二曰割牲。

translations.literal: Twelfth: dismembering victims.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth topic is butchering the victims.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·司士》「凡祭祀，帥其屬而割牲，羞俎豆」。

translations.literal: The Zhou li, Director of Victuals: “Whenever there is sacrifice, he leads his subordinates to cut the victims and present the meat on stands and platters.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Office of the Director of Victuals: “At every sacrifice he leads his staff in cutting the victims and setting out the meat on stands and platters.”

sentences.zh: 又《諸子》，「大祭祀正六牲之體」。

translations.literal: The Record of Various Offices: “At the grand sacrifice he corrects the bodies of the six victims.”
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Various Offices: “At the grand sacrifice he portions the six victims correctly.”

sentences.zh: 《禮運》云「腥其俎，熟其殽，體其犬豕牛羊」。

translations.literal: The Evolution of Rites says: “Set out raw meat on the stands, cook the dishes, and portion the dogs, pigs, cattle, and sheep.”
translations.idiomatic: The Evolution of Rites says: “Place raw portions on the stands, cook the dishes, and joint the dog, pig, cattle, and sheep.”

sentences.zh: 註云：「腥其俎，謂豚解而腥之，為七體也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: “‘Set out raw meat on the stands’ means to butcher a piglet and present it raw, making seven portions.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains: “‘Raw on the stands’ means a piglet jointed while still uncooked into seven portions.

sentences.zh: 熟其殽，謂體解而爓之，為二十一體也。

translations.literal: “Cook the dishes” means to portion the body and simmer it, making twenty-one portions.
translations.idiomatic: “Cook the dishes” means the carcass jointed and simmered into twenty-one portions.

sentences.zh: 體其犬豕牛羊，謂分別骨肉之貴賤，以為眾俎也。」

translations.literal: Portion the dogs, pigs, cattle, and sheep” means to distinguish the noble and humble parts of flesh and bone for the many stands.”
translations.idiomatic: Joint dog, pig, cattle, and sheep” means sorting flesh and bone by rank for the many offering stands.”

sentences.zh: 七體，謂脊、兩肩、兩拍、兩髀。

translations.literal: The seven portions are: spine, two shoulders, two ribs, two thighs.
translations.idiomatic: The seven portions are the spine, both shoulders, both midribs, and both thighs.

sentences.zh: 二十一體，謂肩、臂、臑、膊、骼、正脊、脠脊、橫脊、正脅、短脅、代脅並腸三、胃三、拒肺一、祭肺三也。

translations.literal: The twenty-one portions are: shoulder, arm, foreshank, breast, blade, central spine, tail spine, cross spine, central rib, short rib, substitute rib, together with three intestines, three stomachs, one rejecting lung, and three offering lungs.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-one portions comprise shoulder, arm, shank, breast, blade, central spine, tail spine, cross spine, central rib, short rib, substitute rib, three intestines, three stomachs, one “rejecting” lung, and three lungs for offering.

sentences.zh: 宋元豐三年，詳定禮文所言，古者祭祀用牲，有豚解，有體解。

translations.literal: What the Yuanfeng 3 ritual text revision of the Song states: in antiquity sacrifices used victims with piglet jointing and with body jointing.
translations.idiomatic: The Song’s the third year of Yuanfeng ritual revision notes that ancient sacrifices employed piglet jointing and full carcass jointing.

sentences.zh: 豚解則為七，以薦腥；

translations.literal: Piglet jointing yields seven, presented as raw offering;
translations.idiomatic: Piglet jointing produced seven pieces for the raw offering;

sentences.zh: 體解則為二十一，以薦熟。

translations.literal: Body jointing yields twenty-one, presented as cooked offering.
translations.idiomatic: Full jointing produced twenty-one for the cooked offering.

sentences.zh: 蓋犬豕牛羊，分別骨肉貴賤，其解之為體，則均也。

translations.literal: For dogs, pigs, cattle, and sheep, distinguishing noble and humble flesh and bone—the jointing into portions is the same in principle.
translations.idiomatic: For dog, pig, cattle, and sheep alike, rank distinguished flesh and bone, but the principle of jointing was the same.

sentences.zh: 皇朝馬牛羊豕鹿，並依至大三年割牲用國禮。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, horse, cattle, sheep, pig, and deer all follow the Zhida 3 dismembering according to the national rite.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty butchers horse, cattle, sheep, pig, and deer by the Zhida 3 national rite.

sentences.zh: 圓議依舊儀。

translations.literal: The collegiate deliberation followed the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat decision kept the old rite.

sentences.zh: 十三曰大次、小次。

translations.literal: Thirteenth: great tent and small tent.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteenth topic is the great and small resting tents.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·掌次》，「王旅上帝，張氈按皇邸。」

translations.literal: Zhou li, Keeper of Tents: “When the king journeys to serve the Supreme Lord, he spreads felt and sets the imperial pavilion.”
translations.idiomatic: The Keeper of Tents in the Rites of Zhou: “When the king journeys to serve Heaven, he spreads felt and erects the imperial pavilion.”

sentences.zh: 唐《通典》前祀三日，尚舍直長施大次於外壝東門之內道北，南向。

translations.literal: Tang Tongdian: three days before the sacrifice, the director of the Palace Provisioners erects the great tent inside the outer enclosure’s east gate on the north side of the path, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Tongdian: three days before the rite the palace provisioners set the great tent inside the east gate of the outer moat, north of the path, facing south.

sentences.zh: 《宋會要》前祀三日，儀鸞司帥其屬，設大次於外壝東門之內道北，南向；

translations.literal: Song Essentials: three days before, the Directorate of Ceremonial Insignia leads its staff to set the great tent inside the outer enclosure’s east gate on the north side of the path, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: The Song Essentials: three days beforehand the insignia office set the great tent inside the east gate on the north side, facing south;

sentences.zh: 小次於午階之東，西向。

translations.literal: The small tent east of the noon stair, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: And the small tent east of the south stair, facing west.

sentences.zh: 《曲禮》曰：「踐阼，臨祭祀。」

translations.literal: The Qu li says: “Ascend the stair; preside over sacrifice.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rules of Propriety says: “Mount the stair and preside at sacrifice.”

sentences.zh: 《正義》曰：「阼主階也。

translations.literal: The Correct Meaning says: “Zha is the principal stair.
translations.idiomatic: The Correct Meaning notes: “Zha is the principal stair.

sentences.zh: 天子祭祀履主階行事，故云踐阼。」

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven sacrifices, he treads the principal stair to perform the rites—hence “ascend the stair.”
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven performs sacrifice on the principal stair, hence “ascend the stair.”

sentences.zh: 宋元豐詳定禮文所言，《周禮》宗廟無設小次之文。

translations.literal: What the Yuanfeng Song ritual revision states: in the Zhou li’s ancestral temple there is no passage on setting a small tent.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng ritual revision observed that the Zhou rites for the ancestral temple mention no small tent.

sentences.zh: 古者人君臨位於阼階。

translations.literal: In antiquity the ruler took his place at the zha stair.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity rulers took their place at the principal stair.

sentences.zh: 蓋阼階者，東階也。

translations.literal: The zha stair is the eastern stair.
translations.idiomatic: The principal stair was the eastern stair.

sentences.zh: 惟人主得位主階行事。

translations.literal: Only the ruler could take the principal stair to perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ruler could officiate from the principal stair.

sentences.zh: 今國朝太廟儀註，大次、小次皆在西，蓋國家尚右，以西為尊也。
