translations.literal: In our dynasty’s ancestral temple regulations, both great and small tents are on the west—since the state honors the right and regards west as honored.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestral temple regulations place both tents on the west; the state esteems the right, and west is supreme.

sentences.zh: 圓議依祀廟儀註。

translations.literal: The collegiate deliberation followed the temple-sacrifice regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat followed the temple sacrifice code.

sentences.zh: 續具末議：一曰禮神玉。

translations.literal: Further submitted supplementary proposals: first, jades for honoring the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Further supplementary proposals were submitted. First: jades for honoring the spirits.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·大宗伯》，「以禋祀祀昊天上帝」。

translations.literal: Zhou li, Grand Director of Ritual: “Use the smoke sacrifice to worship the August Heaven, the Supreme Lord.”
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Director of Ritual in the Rites of Zhou: “With the smoke sacrifice worship August Heaven and the Supreme Lord.”

sentences.zh: 註：「禋之言煙也。

translations.literal: Commentary: “Yin means smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary: “Yin means smoke.

sentences.zh: 周人尚臭，煙氣之臭聞者。

translations.literal: The Zhou prized fragrance; they prized the smell borne on smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou prized scent—the odor carried on smoke.

sentences.zh: 積柴實牲體焉，或有玉帛。」

translations.literal: They piled firewood and placed the victim’s flesh on it; sometimes there were also jade and silk.”
translations.idiomatic: They heaped fuel and placed the victim’s flesh upon it; jade and silk might be included.”

sentences.zh: 《正義》曰：「或有玉帛，或不用玉帛，皆不定之辭也。」

translations.literal: The Correct Meaning says: “‘Sometimes jade and silk’ or not using jade and silk—both are indefinite expressions.”
translations.idiomatic: The Correct Meaning: “Whether jade and silk were used is left indefinite in the text.”

sentences.zh: 崔氏雲，天子自奉玉帛牲體於柴上，引《詩》「圭璧既卒」，是燔牲玉也。

translations.literal: Master Cui says the Son of Heaven himself presented jade, silk, and the victim’s flesh on the pyre, citing the Ode “The jade tablets are complete”—thus burning victim and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Cui argued that the Son of Heaven laid jade, silk, and flesh on the pyre, citing “The tablets are complete”—hence burning victim and jade together.

sentences.zh: 蓋卒者，終也。

translations.literal: “Complete” means finished.
translations.idiomatic: “Complete” means finished.

sentences.zh: 謂禮神既終，當藏之也。

translations.literal: It means that when honoring the spirits is finished, they should be stored away.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, the jades were to be stored away.

sentences.zh: 正經即無燔玉明證。

translations.literal: The canonical text itself has no clear proof of burning jade.
translations.idiomatic: The canonical text offers no clear proof of burning jade.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝祠太乙，胙餘皆燔之，無玉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han sacrificed to the Great One; the remaining portions were all burned—no jade.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu worshipped the Great One, leftover portions were burned—but not jade.

sentences.zh: 晉燔牲幣，無玉。

translations.literal: Jin burned victims and silks; no jade.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin burned victims and silks, not jade.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋乃有之。

translations.literal: Only Tang and Song had it.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Tang and Song did the practice appear.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，許敬宗等修舊禮，乃雲郊天之有四圭，猶宗廟之有圭瓚也，並事畢收藏，不在燔列。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era, Xu Jingzong and others revised the old rites and said: the four tablets for suburban Heaven are like the tablet and libation cup in the ancestral temple—all stored after the rite, not placed among what is burned.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing, Xu Jingzong’s ritual revision compared the four suburban jades to the temple tablet and libation cup: all were stored after the rite, never burned.

sentences.zh: 宋政和禮制局言：「古祭祀無不用玉，《周官》典瑞掌玉器之藏，蓋事已則藏焉，有事則出而復用，未嘗有燔瘞之文。

translations.literal: Song Zhenghe Ritual Bureau said: “In antiquity no sacrifice omitted jade. The Zhou’s Director of Regalia kept jade in store—when the affair ended they were stored; when needed they were taken out and used again. There is never text on burning or burying them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Zhenghe Ritual Bureau argued: “Ancient sacrifice always used jade. The Director of Regalia kept them in store, bringing them out when needed; the classics never mention burning or burying them.

sentences.zh: 今後大祀，禮神之玉時出而用，無得燔瘞。」

translations.literal: Henceforth at grand sacrifices, the jades for honoring the spirits shall be brought out as needed and used; they must not be burned or buried.”
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at grand sacrifices the spirit jades are to be brought out when needed, never burned or buried.”

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 蓋燔者取其煙氣之臭聞。

translations.literal: Burning is to take the fragrance of the smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Burning was meant for the scent carried on smoke.

sentences.zh: 玉既無煙，又且無氣，祭之日但當奠於神座，既卒事，則收藏之。

translations.literal: Jade has neither smoke nor vapor; on the day of sacrifice it should only be set before the spirit seat, and when the affair is finished, stored away.
translations.idiomatic: Jade gives off neither smoke nor vapor; on the sacrifice day it is set before the spirit seat, then stored when the rite is done.

sentences.zh: 三曰升煙。

translations.literal: Third: raising smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Third: raising smoke.

sentences.zh: 禋之言煙也，升煙所以報陽也。

translations.literal: Yin means smoke; raising smoke is how yang is acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: Yin means smoke; raising smoke acknowledges the yang principle.

sentences.zh: 祀天之有禋柴，猶祭地之瘞血，宗廟之祼鬯。

translations.literal: The smoke sacrifice and fuel pyre for Heaven are like burying blood for Earth and the libation pour in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s smoke and pyre correspond to burying blood for Earth and pouring libation in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 歷代以來，或先燔而後祭，或先祭而後燔，皆為未允。

translations.literal: Through the ages, some burned first then sacrificed, some sacrificed first then burned—none is satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: Through the ages some burned before sacrificing and some after—both orders were flawed.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，樂六變而燔牲首，牲首亦陽也。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, when the music had changed six times they burned the victim’s head—the head too is yang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice, after six musical changes they burned the victim’s head, for the head too belongs to yang.

sentences.zh: 祭終，以爵酒饌物及牲體，燎於壇。

translations.literal: When sacrifice ended, wine from the cup, viands, and victim’s flesh were burned on the altar mound.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, cup-wine, food, and flesh were burned on the altar.

sentences.zh: 天子望燎，柴用柏。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven gazed upon the burning; cypress was used for fuel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor watched the blaze; cypress served as fuel.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太皇太后崩，有旨冬至南郊祀事，可權止。

translations.literal: That year the Grand Empress Dowager died; an edict said the winter solstice southern suburban sacrifice could be provisionally halted.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after the Grand Empress Dowager’s death, an edict suspended the winter solstice suburban sacrifice for the time being.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年春正月，御史臺臣言：「自世祖迄英宗，咸未親郊，惟武宗、英宗親享太廟，陛下宜躬祀郊廟。」

translations.literal: First month, spring, fourth year of Taiding: censorate officials said: “From Shizu to Yingzong, none personally performed suburban sacrifice; only Wuzong and Yingzong personally enjoyed the ancestral temple. Your Majesty should personally sacrifice at suburb and temple.”
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Taiding 4 the censorate urged: “From Kublai through Yingzong no emperor personally performed the suburban rite; only Wuzong and Yingzong attended the ancestral temple in person. Your Majesty should sacrifice at suburb and temple yourself.”

sentences.zh: 制曰：「朕當遵世祖舊典，其命大臣攝行祀事。」

translations.literal: An edict said: “We shall follow Shizu’s old precedent; let ministers be ordered to perform the sacrifices by proxy.”
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: “I shall follow Kublai’s precedent and have ministers perform the rites in my stead.”

sentences.zh: 閏九月甲戌，郊祀天地，致祭五嶽四瀆、名山大川。

translations.literal: Intercalary ninth month, day jiaxu: suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; offerings sent to the Five Peaks, Four Rivers, and famous mountains and great streams.
translations.idiomatic: On intercalary 9/19 the court sacrificed to Heaven and Earth and made offerings to the Five Peaks, Four Rivers, and the great mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，文宗將親郊。

translations.literal: First year of Zhishun: Wenzong was about to perform suburban sacrifice in person.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 Emperor Wenzong prepared to conduct the suburban rite in person.

sentences.zh: 十月辛亥，太常博士言：「親祀儀註已具，事有未盡者，按前代典禮。

translations.literal: Tenth month, day xinhai: a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: “The regulations for personal sacrifice are ready; where matters remain incomplete, consult former dynasties’ canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: On 10/xinhai a ritual erudite reported: “The code for personal sacrifice is in place; where it is still incomplete, consult earlier dynastic precedents.

sentences.zh: 親郊七日，百官習儀於郊壇。

translations.literal: Seven days before personal suburban sacrifice, all officials practice the rite at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days before the emperor’s suburban rite all officials rehearsed at the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 今既與受戒誓相妨，合於致齋前一日，告示與祭執事者，各具公服赴南郊習儀。

translations.literal: Now it conflicts with receiving the oath of abstinence; it should be fixed for the day before rigorous abstinence, notifying those who officiate at sacrifice each to wear official dress and go to the southern suburb to practice the rite.
translations.idiomatic: This now clashes with the abstinence oath; rehearsal should move to the day before rigorous abstinence, with all officiants notified to appear at the southern suburb in court dress.

sentences.zh: 親祀太廟雖有防禁，然郊外尤宜嚴戒，往來貴乎清肅。

translations.literal: Personal sacrifice at the ancestral temple has prohibitions, yet outside the city especially should be strictly guarded; comings and goings should be pure and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple rite has its guards, but the suburban precinct demands even stricter discipline and austere comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 凡與祭執事齋郎樂工，舊不設盥洗之位，殊非涓潔之道。

translations.literal: All who officiate at sacrifice—attendants, abstainers, musicians—formerly had no places for hand-washing, which is far from the way of meticulous purity.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice officiants, abstainers, and musicians had no hand-washing stations—hardly meticulous purity.

sentences.zh: 今合於饌殿齊班廳前及齋宿之所，隨宜設置盥洗數處，俱用鍋釜溫水置盆杓巾帨，令人掌管省諭，必盥洗然後行事，違者治之。

translations.literal: Now at the viand hall, before the assembly hall, and at lodging for abstention, hand-washing stations should be set as appropriate in several places, all with cauldrons of warm water, basins, ladles, towels, and cloths, with persons assigned to supervise and announce—all must wash before performing rites; violators punished.
translations.idiomatic: Washing stations with warm water, basins, ladles, and towels should be set at the viand hall, assembly hall, and lodgings, with supervisors ensuring everyone washed before serving; violators were to be punished.

sentences.zh: 祭日，太常院分官提調神廚，監視割烹。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were assigned to supervise the spirit kitchen and oversee cutting and cooking.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day the Court of Imperial Sacrifices posted officers to supervise the spirit kitchen and butchering.

sentences.zh: 上下燈燭籸燎，已前雖有翦燭提調籸盆等官，率皆虛應故事；

translations.literal: For lamps, candles, grain torches, and burning above and below, although there were officials for trimming candles and supervising grain basins, they mostly went through the motions per precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Though officials nominally trimmed candles and tended grain offerings for the upper and lower lamps, most merely went through the motions;

sentences.zh: 或減刻物料，燭燎不明。

translations.literal: Sometimes they reduced materials, so lamps and burning were dim.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes skimping on supplies left the altar poorly lit.

sentences.zh: 又嘗見奉禮贊賜胙之後，獻官方退，所司便服徹俎，壇上燈燭一時俱滅，因而雜人登壇攘奪，不能禁止，甚為褻慢。

translations.literal: Moreover it was once seen that after the ritual officer praised the grant of flesh and the offering officials had withdrawn, the responsible offices in ordinary dress cleared the stands, all lamps on the altar were extinguished at once, and thus common people climbed the altar and snatched offerings—could not be stopped—highly profane.
translations.idiomatic: After the blessing of sacrificial flesh, offering officials would withdraw while attendants in plain dress cleared the stands and doused every lamp—letting commoners swarm the altar unchecked, a grave profanation.

sentences.zh: 今宜禁約，省牲之前，凡入壝門之人，皆服窄紫，有官者公服。

translations.literal: Now restrictions should be imposed: before inspecting the victims, all who enter the enclosure gate must wear narrow purple; those with office wear court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Restrictions should bar anyone entering the enclosure before the victim inspection unless dressed in narrow purple; officers in court dress.

sentences.zh: 禁治四壝紅門，宜令所司添造關木鎖鑰，祭畢即令關閉，毋使雜人得入。

translations.literal: The four enclosure red gates should be secured: the responsible offices should add gate bars and locks; when sacrifice ends they should be closed at once, not letting common people enter.
translations.idiomatic: The four red gates of the enclosure should be fitted with bars and locks and shut the moment the rite ended, barring unauthorized entry.

sentences.zh: 其稿稭匏爵，事畢合依大德九年例焚之。」

translations.literal: Straw, stalks, and gourd cups, when the affair is finished, should all be burned according to the ninth year of Dade precedent.”
translations.idiomatic: Straw, stalks, and gourd libation cups should be burned afterward per the Dade 9 precedent.”

sentences.zh: 壬子，御史臺臣言：「祭日，宜敕股肱近臣及諸執事人毋飲酒。」

translations.literal: Day renzi: censorate officials said: “On the sacrifice day, close ministers and all who officiate should be ordered not to drink wine.”
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the censorate urged: “On the sacrifice day forbid wine to the emperor’s nearest ministers and all ritual officiants.”

sentences.zh: 制曰：「卿言甚善，其移文中書禁之。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your words are very good; issue a document through the Secretariat forbidding it."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Your advice is excellent. Have the Secretariat issue a prohibition."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，監察御史楊彬等言：「禮，享帝必以始祖為配，今未聞設配位，竊恐禮文有闕。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Supervising Censor Yang Bin and others said: "In ritual, when sacrificing to the Emperor one must have the founding ancestor as associate; we have not heard that an associate seat has been set up—we fear the ritual text is incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Supervising Censor Yang Bin and others memorialized: "Ritual requires that sacrifice to the Lord on High be accompanied by the founding ancestor. No associate seat has been announced, and we fear the rite is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 又，先祀一日，皇帝必備法駕出宿郊次，其扈從近侍之臣未嘗經歷，宜申加戒敕，以達孚誠。」

translations.literal: Moreover, one day before the sacrifice the emperor must fully equip the imperial carriage and go out to lodge at the suburban station; the close ministers in his escort have not experienced this before—they should be admonished and instructed so as to achieve sincere devotion."
translations.idiomatic: They also urged that on the eve of the rite the emperor must ride out in full state to lodge at the suburban station. Many in the escort would be inexperienced; they should receive strict admonition so the court’s sincerity would be plain."

sentences.zh: 命與中書議行。

translations.literal: An order was given to discuss and implement it with the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Secretariat to deliberate and carry this out.

sentences.zh: 十月辛酉，始服大裘袞冕，親祀昊天上帝於南郊，以太祖配。

translations.literal: In the tenth month on xinyou, for the first time he wore the great fur robe and full regalia and personally sacrificed to August Heaven at the southern suburb, with Taizu as associate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on the day xinyou, he first donned the great fur robe and full court regalia and personally offered to August Heaven at the southern suburb, with Taizu as associate.

sentences.zh: 自世祖混一六合，至文宗凡七世，而南郊親祀之禮始克舉焉，蓋器物儀註至是益加詳慎矣。

translations.literal: From Shizu’s unification of the realm to Wenzong was seven generations in all, yet only then could the rite of personal sacrifice at the southern suburb be carried out—for implements, vessels, and ritual regulations had by then become ever more detailed and careful.
translations.idiomatic: From Kublai’s unification through seven reigns to Wenzong, the southern-suburb rite in the emperor’s own person could be performed only now, when vessels, regalia, and ritual directions had at last been refined with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 自至元十二年冬十二月，用香酒脯臡行一獻禮。

translations.literal: From the twelfth month of winter in the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, fragrant wine, dried meat, and minced offerings were used to perform the single-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: From the winter of Zhiyuan 12, the rite used fragrant wine with dried and minced meats in a single offering.

sentences.zh: 而至治元年冬二祭告，泰定元年之正月，咸用之。

translations.literal: For the two winter announcement sacrifices of Zhizhi 1 and the first month of Taiding 1, all used them as well.
translations.idiomatic: The same provisions served the two winter announcement sacrifices of Zhizhi 1 and the first month of Taiding 1.

sentences.zh: 自大德九年冬至，用純色馬一，蒼犢一，羊鹿野豕各九。

translations.literal: From the winter solstice of Dade 9, there were one horse of pure color, one dark calf, and nine each of sheep, deer, and wild boar.
translations.idiomatic: From the Dade 9 winter solstice onward, offerings included one pure-colored horse, one dark calf, and nine each of sheep, deer, and wild boar.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋七月，用馬一，蒼犢正副各一，羊鹿野豕各九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of year 11, there were one horse, one principal and one associate dark calf, and nine each of sheep, deer, and wild boar.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 11, the tally was one horse, principal and associate dark calves, and nine each of sheep, deer, and wild boar.

sentences.zh: 而至大中告謝五，皇慶至延祐告謝七，與至治三年冬告謝二，泰定元年之二月，咸如大德十一年之數。

translations.literal: For the five announcement-and-thanks rites of Dazhong, the seven from Huangqing through Yanyou, the two winter announcement-and-thanks of Zhizhi 3, and the second month of Taiding 1—all followed the quantities of Dade 11.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong’s five thanksgiving rites, Huangqing–Yanyou’s seven, Zhizhi 3’s two winter thanksgivings, and Taiding 1’s second month all matched the Dade 11 scale.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年閏九月，特加皇地祇黃犢一，將祀之夕敕送新獵鹿二。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month of Taiding 4, a yellow calf for Imperial Earth was specially added; on the eve of the sacrifice an edict sent two newly hunted deer.
translations.idiomatic: Taiding 4’s intercalary ninth month added a yellow calf for Imperial Earth; on the eve of sacrifice the throne ordered two freshly hunted deer delivered.

sentences.zh: 惟至大三年冬至，正配位蒼犢皆一，五方帝犢各一，皆如其方之色，大明青犢、夜明白犢皆一，馬一，羊鹿野豕各十有八，兔十有二，而四年四月如之。

translations.literal: Only at the winter solstice of Zhida 3: one dark calf each for principal and associate seats, one calf each for the Five Directional Emperors—all in each direction’s color; one green calf for Great Brightness and one white for Night Brightness; one horse; eighteen each of sheep, deer, and wild boar; twelve hares—and in the fourth month of year 4 it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Zhida 3’s winter solstice alone used one dark calf each for the principal and associate, one directional calf per Five Emperor (in each direction’s color), one green calf for Great Brightness and one white for Night Brightness, one horse, eighteen each of sheep, deer, and wild boar, and twelve hares—the fourth month of year 4 repeated this.

sentences.zh: 其犧牲品物香酒，皆參用國禮，而豐約不同。

translations.literal: Sacrificial victims, offerings, and fragrant wine all drew on state ritual, but fullness or economy differed.
translations.idiomatic: Victims, offerings, and fragrant wine followed state ritual, though scale varied between lavish and modest occasions.

sentences.zh: 告謝非大祀，而用物無異，豈所謂未能一舉而大備者乎？

translations.literal: Announcement-and-thanks was not a great sacrifice, yet the materials used were no different—is this not what is meant by being unable to accomplish all at once and prepare fully?
translations.idiomatic: Thanksgiving rites were not great sacrifices, yet their provisions matched them—perhaps this is what “unable to prepare everything at once” meant.

sentences.zh: 南郊之禮，其始為告祭，繼而有大祀，皆攝事也，故攝祀之儀特詳。

translations.literal: The southern-suburb rite began as announcement sacrifice, then came great sacrifice; all were conducted by proxy, so regulations for proxy sacrifice are especially detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Southern-suburb worship began with announcement sacrifices and later included great sacrifices, all initially by proxy—hence the unusually full rules for proxy rites.

sentences.zh: 壇壝：地在麗正門外丙位，凡三百八畝有奇。

translations.literal: Altar and enclosure: the site lay in the bing position outside Lizheng Gate, more than 308 mu in all.
translations.idiomatic: Altar and precinct: the ground stood in the bing quarter southeast of Lizheng Gate, over 308 mu in extent.

sentences.zh: 壇三成，每成高八尺一寸，上成縱橫五丈，中成十丈，下成十五丈。

translations.literal: The altar had three tiers; each tier was eight chi one cun high; the upper tier five zhang square, the middle ten zhang, the lower fifteen zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The altar rose in three terraces, each 8 chi 1 cun high: the top 5 zhang square, the middle 10, the base 15.

sentences.zh: 四陛午貫地子午卯酉四位陛十有二級。

translations.literal: Four ramps aligned at noon through the earth—at the four positions zi, wu, mao, and you—each of twelve steps.
translations.idiomatic: Four stairways pierced the mound on the zi, wu, mao, and you axes, each with twelve steps.

sentences.zh: 外設二壝。

translations.literal: Two enclosures were set outside.
translations.idiomatic: Two walled enclosures lay outside the altar.

sentences.zh: 內壝去壇二十五步，外壝去內壝五十四步。

translations.literal: The inner enclosure stood twenty-five paces from the altar; the outer enclosure fifty-four paces from the inner.
translations.idiomatic: The inner wall was 25 paces from the altar; the outer wall 54 paces beyond the inner.

sentences.zh: 壝各四門，外垣南欞星門三，東西欞星門各一。

translations.literal: Each enclosure had four gates; on the outer wall were three Lattice Star Gates to the south and one each east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Each precinct had four gates; the outer wall had three Lattice Star Gates on the south and one each on east and west.

sentences.zh: 圜壇周圍上下俱護以甓，內外壝各高五尺，壝四面各有門三，俱塗以赤。

translations.literal: The round altar was walled all around with brick above and below; inner and outer enclosures were each five chi high; each face of each enclosure had three gates, all painted red.
translations.idiomatic: Brick revetments ringed the round altar top and bottom. Inner and outer walls stood 5 chi high, each side with three gates painted red.

sentences.zh: 至大三年冬至，以三成不足以容從祀版位，以青繩代一成。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of Zhida 3, because three tiers could not hold the associated spirit tablets, a blue rope stood in for one tier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhida 3’s winter solstice: three terraces could not fit all associated tablets, so a blue cord marked a fourth tier.

sentences.zh: 繩二百，各長二十五尺，以足四成之制。

translations.literal: Two hundred ropes, each twenty-five chi long, to complete the four-tier design.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred cords, each 25 chi long, completed the four-terrace layout.

sentences.zh: 燎壇在外壝內丙巳之位，高一丈二尺，四方各一丈，周圜亦護以甓，東西南三出陛，開上南出戶，上方六尺，深可容柴。

translations.literal: The fire altar stood within the outer enclosure at the bingsi position, one zhang two chi high and one zhang square; it too was walled with brick. Ramps led out on east, south, and west; an opening above had a southern door. The mouth was six chi across and deep enough for firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the outer wall at bingsi stood the fire altar: 1 zhang 2 chi high, 1 zhang square, brick-lined, with ramps on three sides and a southern hatch 6 chi wide, deep enough for fuel.

sentences.zh: 香殿三間，在外壝南門之外，少西，南向。

translations.literal: Incense hall, three bays, outside the south gate of the outer enclosure, slightly west, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: A three-bay incense hall stood just west of the outer south gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 饌幕殿五間，在外壝南門之外，少東，南向。

translations.literal: Food-pavilion hall, five bays, outside the south gate of the outer enclosure, slightly east, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: A five-bay offering pavilion stood just east of the outer south gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 省饌殿一間，在外壝東門之外，少北，南向。

translations.literal: Victual-inspection hall, one bay, outside the east gate of the outer enclosure, slightly north, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: A one-bay inspection hall stood just north of the outer east gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 外壝之東南為別院。

translations.literal: Southeast of the outer enclosure was a separate compound.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the outer precinct lay a detached yard.

sentences.zh: 內神廚五間，南向；

translations.literal: Inner spirit kitchen, five bays, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: an inner spirit kitchen of five bays, south-facing;

sentences.zh: 祠祭局三間，北向；

translations.literal: sacrifice administration office, three bays, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: a three-bay sacrifice office, north-facing;

sentences.zh: 酒庫三間，西向。

translations.literal: wine storehouse, three bays, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: and a three-bay wine store, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 獻官齋房二十間，在神廚南垣之外，西向。

translations.literal: Offering-official fasting chambers, twenty bays, outside the south wall of the spirit kitchen, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty bays of fasting rooms for offering officials lay west of the spirit kitchen’s south wall.

sentences.zh: 外壝南門之外，為中神門五間，諸執事齋房六十間以翼之，皆北向。

translations.literal: Outside the south gate of the outer enclosure was the central spirit gate of five bays, with sixty fasting chambers for all attending officers flanking it—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the outer south gate stood a five-bay central spirit gate flanked by sixty service fasting rooms, all facing north.

sentences.zh: 兩翼端皆有垣，以抵東西周垣，各為門，以便出入。

translations.literal: At both wing ends were walls reaching the east and west perimeter walls, each with a gate for convenient passage.
translations.idiomatic: Wing walls met the east and west perimeter, each with a gate for passage.

sentences.zh: 齊班廳五間，在獻官齋房之前，西向。

translations.literal: Formation hall, five bays, before the offering-official fasting chambers, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: A five-bay mustering hall stood west of the offering officials’ fasting rooms.

sentences.zh: 儀鸞局三間，法物庫三間，都監庫五間，在外垣內之西北隅，皆西向。

translations.literal: Ceremonial guard bureau three bays, ritual-objects store three bays, chief supervision store five bays—in the northwest corner within the outer wall, all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the northwest within the outer wall: three bays for the ceremonial guard, three for ritual stores, five for the chief depot—all west-facing.

sentences.zh: 雅樂庫十間，在外垣西門之內，少南，東向。

translations.literal: Elegant music store, ten bays, inside the west gate of the outer wall, slightly south, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: A ten-bay court-music store stood inside the west gate, slightly south, facing east.

sentences.zh: 演樂堂七間，在外垣內之西南隅，東向。

translations.literal: Music-rehearsal hall, seven bays, in the southwest corner within the outer wall, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: A seven-bay rehearsal hall occupied the inner southwest corner, facing east.

sentences.zh: 獻官廚三間，在外垣內之東南隅，西向。

translations.literal: Offering-official kitchen, three bays, in the southeast corner within the outer wall, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: A three-bay kitchen for offering officials stood in the inner southeast, facing west.

sentences.zh: 滌養犧牲所，在外垣南門之外，少東，西向。

translations.literal: Place for washing and raising sacrificial animals, outside the south gate of the outer wall, slightly east, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The wash and holding pens for victims lay east of the outer south gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 內犧牲房三間，南向。

translations.literal: Inner sacrificial-animal pens, three bays, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Inner victim pens of three bays faced south.

sentences.zh: 神位：昊天上帝位天壇之中，少北，皇地祇位次東，少卻，皆南向。

translations.literal: Spirit seats: August Heaven in the center of the heaven altar, slightly north; Imperial Earth next to the east, slightly withdrawn—both facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit seats: August Heaven at the altar’s center, slightly north; Imperial Earth east and a step back—both south-facing.

sentences.zh: 神席皆緣以繒，綾褥素座，昊天上帝色皆用青，皇地祇色皆用黃，藉皆以稿稭。

translations.literal: Spirit mats were bordered with silk, brocade cushions on plain seats; for August Heaven all colors were blue, for Imperial Earth yellow; all were padded with straw.
translations.idiomatic: Mats were silk-edged with brocade cushions on plain bases—blue for Heaven, yellow for Earth—straw underneath.

sentences.zh: 配位居東，西向。

translations.literal: The associate seat was to the east, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The associate stood east of the altar, facing west.

sentences.zh: 神席綾褥錦方座，色皆用青，藉以蒲越。

translations.literal: Spirit mat: brocade cushion on brocade square seat, all blue, padded with rush mat.
translations.idiomatic: Its mat used brocade on a brocade square seat in blue, with rush padding.

sentences.zh: 其從祀圜壇，第一等九位。

translations.literal: For associated sacrifice at the round altar, the first rank had nine seats.
translations.idiomatic: At the round altar, first-rank associated spirits numbered nine.

sentences.zh: 青帝位寅，赤帝位巳，黃帝位未，白帝位申，黑帝位亥，主皆用柏，素質玄書；

translations.literal: Green Emperor at yin, Red at si, Yellow at wei, White at shen, Black at hai—the tablets all of cypress with plain bodies and black characters;
translations.idiomatic: Green Emperor at yin, Red at si, Yellow at wei, White at shen, Black at hai—cypress tablets, plain wood, black script;

sentences.zh: 大明位卯，夜明位酉，北極位醜，天皇大帝位戌，用神位版，丹質黃書。

translations.literal: Great Brightness at mao, Night Brightness at you, Northern Pole at chou, Celestial Emperor at xu—they used spirit tablets of red body with yellow characters.
translations.idiomatic: Great Brightness at mao, Night Brightness at you, Northern Pole at chou, Celestial Emperor at xu—red tablets with yellow script.

sentences.zh: 神席綾褥座各隨其方色，藉皆以稿稭。

translations.literal: Spirit mats and brocade cushion-seats each followed the color of its direction; all were padded with straw.
translations.idiomatic: Mats and cushions matched each direction’s color, straw underneath.

sentences.zh: 第二等內官位五十有四。

translations.literal: The second rank: inner asterisms, fifty-four seats.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: inner asterisms—fifty-four seats.

sentences.zh: 鉤星、天柱、玄枵、天廚、柱史位於子，其數五；

translations.literal: Gouxing, Tianzhu, Xuanxiao, Tianchu, and Zhishi at zi—five in number;
translations.idiomatic: At zi: Gou Star, Celestial Pillar, Rooftop, Celestial Kitchen, and Pillar Scribe—five;

sentences.zh: 女史、星紀、御女位於醜，其數三；

translations.literal: Nüshi, Xingji, and Yunu at chou—three in number;
translations.idiomatic: at chou: Woman Scribe, Star Record, and Serving Maid—three;

sentences.zh: 自子至醜，神位皆西上。

translations.literal: From zi to chou, all spirit seats faced west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from zi through chou, seats ranked west at the top.

sentences.zh: 帝座、歲星、大理、河漢、析木、尚書位於寅，帝座居前行，其數六，南上。

translations.literal: Di Seat, Year Star, Grand Judge, River Han, Split Wood, and Minister at yin—Di Seat in the front rank, six in number, ranked south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At yin: Imperial Seat, Jupiter, Grand Judge, River Han, Split Wood, and Minister—Imperial Seat foremost, six seats, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 陰德、大火、天槍、玄戈、天床位於卯，其數五，北上。

translations.literal: Yinde, Great Fire, Sky Lance, Black Spear, and Celestial Bed at mao—five in number, ranked north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At mao: Hidden Virtue, Great Fire, Sky Lance, Black Spear, and Celestial Bed—five, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 太陽守、相星、壽星、輔星、三師位於辰，其數五，南上。

translations.literal: Solar Guardian, Chancellor Star, Longevity Star, Assistant Star, and Three Masters at chen—five in number, ranked south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At chen: Solar Guardian, Chancellor, Longevity, Assistant, and Three Masters—five, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 天一、太一、內廚、熒惑、鶉尾、勢星、天理位於巳，天一、太一居前行，其數七，西上。

translations.literal: Tianyi, Taiyi, Inner Kitchen, Spark Star, Quail Tail, Power Star, and Heavenly Principle at si—Tianyi and Taiyi in the front rank, seven in number, ranked west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At si: Celestial One, Supreme One, Inner Kitchen, Mars, Quail Tail, Power Star, and Heavenly Principle—Celestial and Supreme One foremost, seven, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 北斗、天牢、三公、鶉火、文昌、內階位於午，北斗居前行，其數六；

translations.literal: Northern Dipper, Celestial Prison, Three Dukes, Quail Fire, Wenchang, and Inner Steps at wu—Northern Dipper in the front rank, six in number;
translations.idiomatic: At wu: Northern Dipper, Celestial Prison, Three Dukes, Quail Fire, Wenchang, and Inner Steps—Dipper foremost, six;

sentences.zh: 填星、鶉首、四輔位於未，其數三；

translations.literal: Saturn, Quail Head, and Four Assistants at wei—three in number;
translations.idiomatic: at wei: Saturn, Quail Head, and Four Assistants—three;

sentences.zh: 自午至未，皆東上。

translations.literal: From wu to wei, all faced east at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from wu through wei, seats ranked east at the top.

sentences.zh: 太白、實沈位於申，其數二，北上。

translations.literal: Venus and Real Shen at shen—two in number, ranked north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At shen: Venus and Real Shen—two, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 八谷、大梁、杠星、華蓋位於酉，其數四；

translations.literal: Eight Grains, Great Bridge, Pillar Star, and Canopy at you—four in number;
translations.idiomatic: At you: Eight Grains, Great Bridge, Pillar Star, and Canopy—four;

sentences.zh: 五帝內座、降婁、六甲、傳舍位於戌，五帝內座居前行，其數四；

translations.literal: Inner Seats of the Five Emperors, Descending Harvest, Six Jia, and Relay Lodgings at xu—Inner Seats of the Five Emperors in the front rank, four in number;
translations.idiomatic: at xu: Inner Seats of the Five Emperors, Descending Harvest, Six Jia, and Relay Lodgings—Five Emperors foremost, four;

sentences.zh: 自酉至戌，皆南上。

translations.literal: From you to xu, all faced south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from you through xu, seats ranked south at the top.

sentences.zh: 紫微垣、辰星、陬訾、鉤陳位於亥，其數四，東上。

translations.literal: Purple Forbidden Enclosure, Mercury, Zouzi, and Gouchen at hai—four in number, ranked east at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At hai: Purple Forbidden Enclosure, Mercury, Zouzi, and Gouchen—four, east at the top.

sentences.zh: 神席皆藉以莞席，內壝外諸神位皆同。

translations.literal: All spirit mats were padded with sedge mats; all spirit seats within and without the inner enclosure were the same.
translations.idiomatic: All used sedge matting; inner and outer precinct spirits alike.

sentences.zh: 第三等中官百五十九位。

translations.literal: The third rank: middle asterisms, one hundred fifty-nine seats.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: middle asterisms—159 seats.

sentences.zh: 虛宿、女宿、牛宿、織女、人星、司命、司非、司危、司祿、天津、離珠、羅堰、天桴、奚仲、左旗、河鼓、右旗位於子，虛宿、女宿、牛宿、織女居前行，其數十有七；

translations.literal: Void, Woman, Ox, Weaver, Human Star, Director of Fate, Director of Misdeed, Director of Peril, Director of Blessings, Celestial Ford, Pearl at the Ford, Heavenly Raft, Celestial Flute, Xi Zhong, Left Banner, Drum at the River, and Right Banner at zi—Void, Woman, Ox, and Weaver in the front rank, seventeen in number;
translations.idiomatic: At zi: Void, Woman, Ox, Weaver, Human Star, Directors of Fate, Misdeed, Peril, and Blessings, Celestial Ford, Pearl, Raft, Flute, Xi Zhong, Left Banner, River Drum, and Right Banner—Void through Weaver foremost, seventeen;

sentences.zh: 月星、建星、斗宿、箕宿、天雞、輦道、漸臺、敗瓜、扶筐、匏瓜、天弁、天棓、帛度、屠肆、宗星、宗人、宗正位於醜，月星、建星、斗宿、箕宿居前行，其數十有七；

translations.literal: Lunar Star, Establishment Star, Dipper, Winnowing Basket, Celestial Cock, Imperial Road, Ascending Terrace, Defeated Gourd, Basket Bearer, Gourd, Celestial Market, Silk Measure, Butcher’s Shop, Clan Star, Clan Person, and Clan Director at chou—Lunar Star, Establishment Star, Dipper, and Winnowing Basket in the front rank, seventeen in number;
translations.idiomatic: at chou: Moon, Establishment, Dipper, Winnowing Basket, Celestial Cock, Imperial Road, Ascending Terrace, Defeated Gourd, Basket Bearer, Gourd, Market, Silk Measure, Butcher, Clan Star, Clan Person, and Clan Director—Moon through Winnowing Basket foremost, seventeen;

sentences.zh: 自子至醜，皆西上。

translations.literal: From zi to chou, all faced west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from zi through chou, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 日星、心宿、天紀、尾宿、罰星、東咸、列肆、天市垣、斛星、鬥星、車肆、天江、宦星、市樓、候星、女床、天籥位於寅，日星、心宿、天紀、尾宿居前行，其數十有七，南上。

translations.literal: Solar Star, Heart, Heavenly Discipline, Tail, Punishment Star, Eastern Salt, Market Row, Celestial Market Enclosure, Dipper Star, Fight Star, Chariot Quarter, Celestial River, Eunuch Star, Market Tower, Awaiting Star, Woman’s Bed, and Celestial Key at yin—Solar Star, Heart, Heavenly Discipline, and Tail in the front rank, seventeen in number, ranked south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At yin: Sun, Heart, Heavenly Discipline, Tail, Punishment, Eastern Salt, Market Row, Market Enclosure, Dipper, Fight, Chariot Quarter, Celestial River, Eunuch, Market Tower, Awaiting Star, Woman’s Bed, and Celestial Key—Sun through Tail foremost, seventeen, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 房宿、七公、氐宿、帝席、大角、亢宿、貫索、鍵閉、鉤鈐、西咸、天乳、招搖、梗河、亢池、周鼎位於卯，房宿、七公、氐宿、帝席、大角、亢宿居前行，其數十有五，北上。

translations.literal: Room, Seven Lords, Base, Emperor’s Mat, Great Horn, Neck, Coiled Noose, Key Closure, Curved Hook, Western Salt, Celestial Milk, Brandish, Geng River, Neck Pool, and Zhou Tripod at mao—Room, Seven Lords, Base, Emperor’s Mat, Great Horn, and Neck in the front rank, fifteen in number, ranked north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At mao: Room, Seven Lords, Base, Emperor’s Mat, Great Horn, Neck, Coiled Noose, Key Closure, Curved Hook, Western Salt, Celestial Milk, Brandish, Geng River, Neck Pool, and Zhou Tripod—Room through Neck foremost, fifteen, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 太子星、太微垣、軫宿、角宿、攝提、常陳、幸臣、謁者、三公、九卿、五內諸侯、郎位、郎將、進賢、平道、天田位於辰，太子星、太微垣、軫宿、角宿、攝提居前行，其數十有六，南上。

translations.literal: Crown Prince, Supreme Palace Enclosure, Chariot Axle, Horn, Jueti, Regular Array, Favored Minister, Herald, Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, Five Inner Feudatories, Courtier Seats, Courtier General, Advance Worthy, Level Road, and Celestial Field at chen—Crown Prince, Supreme Palace Enclosure, Chariot Axle, Horn, and Jueti in the front rank, sixteen in number, ranked south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At chen: Crown Prince, Supreme Palace, Chariot Axle, Horn, Jueti, Regular Array, Favored Minister, Herald, Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, Five Inner Feudatories, Courtier Seats, Courtier General, Advance Worthy, Level Road, and Celestial Field—Crown Prince through Jueti foremost, sixteen, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 張宿、翼宿、明堂、四帝座、黃帝座、長垣、少微、靈臺、虎賁、從官、內屏位於巳，張宿、翼宿、明堂居前行，其數十有一，西上。

translations.literal: Extended Net, Wings, Bright Hall, Four Thrones, Yellow Emperor’s Seat, Long Wall, Lesser Supreme, Spirit Terrace, Tiger Guard, Attendant Official, and Inner Screen at si—Extended Net, Wings, and Bright Hall in the front rank, eleven in number, ranked west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At si: Extended Net, Wings, Bright Hall, Four Thrones, Yellow Emperor’s Seat, Long Wall, Lesser Supreme, Spirit Terrace, Tiger Guard, Attendant Official, and Inner Screen—Net through Bright Hall foremost, eleven, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 軒轅、七星、三臺、柳宿、內平、太尊、積薪、積水、北河位於午，軒轅、七星、三臺、柳宿居前行，其數九；

translations.literal: Xuanyuan, Seven Stars, Three Terraces, Willow, Inner Level, Grand Honor, Piled Firewood, Piled Water, and North River at wu—Xuanyuan, Seven Stars, Three Terraces, and Willow in the front rank, nine in number;
translations.idiomatic: At wu: Xuanyuan, Seven Stars, Three Terraces, Willow, Inner Level, Grand Honor, Piled Firewood, Piled Water, and North River—Xuanyuan through Willow foremost, nine;

sentences.zh: 鬼宿、井宿、參宿、天尊、五諸侯、鉞星、座旗、司怪、天關位於未，鬼宿、井宿、參宿居前行，其數九；

translations.literal: Ghost, Well, Shen, Celestial Honored, Five Feudatories, Battle-axe Star, Seat Banner, Director of Strange Events, and Celestial Pass at wei—Ghost, Well, and Shen in the front rank, nine in number;
translations.idiomatic: at wei: Ghost, Well, Shen, Celestial Honored, Five Feudatories, Battle-axe, Seat Banner, Director of Strange Events, and Celestial Pass—Ghost through Shen foremost, nine;

sentences.zh: 自午至未，皆東上。

translations.literal: From wu to wei, all faced east at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from wu through wei, east at the top.

sentences.zh: 畢宿、五車、諸王、觜宿、天船、天街、礪石、天高、三柱、天潢、咸池位於申，畢宿、五車、諸王、觜宿居前行，其數十有一，北上。

translations.literal: Net, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Beak, Celestial Boat, Celestial Street, Whetstone, Celestial Height, Three Pillars, Celestial Ford, and Salt Pool at shen—Net, Five Chariots, Various Kings, and Beak in the front rank, eleven in number, ranked north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At shen: Net, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Beak, Celestial Boat, Celestial Street, Whetstone, Celestial Height, Three Pillars, Celestial Ford, and Salt Pool—Net through Beak foremost, eleven, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 月宿、昴宿、胃宿、積水、天讒、卷舌、天河、積屍、太陵、左更、天大將軍、軍南門位於酉，月宿、昴宿、胃宿居前行，其數十有二；

translations.literal: Mao Lodge, Pleiades, Stomach, Piled Water, Celestial Slander, Curled Tongue, Celestial River, Piled Corpses, Great Tomb, Left Deputy, and Great General of Heaven at you—Mao Lodge, Pleiades, and Stomach in the front rank, twelve in number;
translations.idiomatic: At you: Mao Lodge, Pleiades, Stomach, Piled Water, Celestial Slander, Curled Tongue, Celestial River, Piled Corpses, Great Tomb, Left Deputy, and Great General—Mao through Stomach foremost, twelve;

sentences.zh: 婁宿、奎宿、壁宿、右更、附路、閣道、王良、策星、天廄、土公、雲雨、霹靂位於戌，婁宿、壁宿居前行，其數十有二；

translations.literal: Bond, Stride, Wall, Right Deputy, Attached Road, Gallery Road, Wang Liang, Policy Star, Celestial Stable, Earth Duke, Cloud and Rain, and Thunderbolt at xu—Bond and Wall in the front rank, twelve in number;
translations.idiomatic: at xu: Bond, Stride, Wall, Right Deputy, Attached Road, Gallery Road, Wang Liang, Policy Star, Celestial Stable, Earth Duke, Cloud and Rain, and Thunderbolt—Bond and Wall foremost, twelve;

sentences.zh: 自酉至戌，皆南上。

translations.literal: From you to xu, all faced south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from you through xu, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 危宿、室宿、車府、墳墓、虛梁、蓋屋、臼星、杵星、土公吏、造父、離宮、雷電、騰蛇位於亥，危宿、室宿居前行，其數十有三，東上。

translations.literal: Rooftop, Room, Chariot Office, Tomb, Hollow Beam, Covering House, Mortar Star, Pestle Star, Earth Duke Clerk, Zaofu, Detached Palace, Thunder and Lightning, and Soaring Serpent at hai—Rooftop and Room in the front rank, thirteen in number, ranked east at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At hai: Rooftop, Room, Chariot Office, Tomb, Hollow Beam, Covering House, Mortar, Pestle, Earth Duke Clerk, Zaofu, Detached Palace, Thunder and Lightning, and Soaring Serpent—Rooftop and Room foremost, thirteen, east at the top.

sentences.zh: 內壝內外官一百六位。

translations.literal: Within and without the inner enclosure: outer asterisms, one hundred six seats.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the inner wall: outer asterisms—106 seats.

sentences.zh: 天壘城、離瑜、代星、齊星、周星、晉星、韓星、秦星、魏星、燕星、楚星、鄭星位於子，其數十有二；

translations.literal: Celestial Rampart, Liyu, Substitute Star, Qi Star, Zhou Star, Jin Star, Han Star, Qin Star, Wei Star, Yan Star, Chu Star, and Zheng Star at zi—twelve in number;
translations.idiomatic: At zi: Celestial Rampart, Liyu, Substitute, Qi, Zhou, Jin, Han, Qin, Wei, Yan, Chu, and Zheng—twelve;

sentences.zh: 越星、趙星、九坎、天田、狗國、天淵、狗星、鱉星、農丈人、杵星、糠星位於醜，其數十有一；

translations.literal: Yue Star, Zhao Star, Nine Pits, Celestial Field, Dog Country, Celestial Abyss, Dog Star, Turtle Star, Old Farmer, Pestle Star, and Chaff Star at chou—eleven in number;
translations.idiomatic: at chou: Yue, Zhao, Nine Pits, Celestial Field, Dog Country, Celestial Abyss, Dog, Turtle, Old Farmer, Pestle, and Chaff—eleven;

sentences.zh: 自子至醜，皆西上。

translations.literal: From zi to chou, all faced west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: from zi through chou, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 騎陣將軍、天輻、從官、積卒、神宮、傅說、龜星、魚星位於寅，其數八，南上。

translations.literal: Cavalry General, Celestial Spoke, Attendant Official, Piled Soldiers, Spirit Palace, Fu Yue, Turtle Star, and Fish Star at yin—eight in number, ranked south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At yin: Cavalry General, Celestial Spoke, Attendant Official, Piled Soldiers, Spirit Palace, Fu Yue, Turtle, and Fish—eight, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 陣車、車騎、騎官、頡頏、折威、陽門、五柱、天門、衡星、庫樓位於卯，其數十，北上。

translations.literal: Battle Array, Chariot Cavalry, Cavalry Officer, Jiehan, Broken Halberd, Yang Gate, Five Pillars, Celestial Gate, Balance Star, and Arsenal at mao—ten in number, ranked north at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At mao: Battle Array, Chariot Cavalry, Cavalry Officer, Jiehan, Broken Halberd, Yang Gate, Five Pillars, Celestial Gate, Balance, and Arsenal—ten, north at the top.

sentences.zh: 土司空、長沙、青丘、南門、平星位於辰，其數五，南上。

translations.literal: Earth Minister, Changsha, Green Hill, Southern Gate, and Level Star at chen—five in number, ranked south at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At chen: Earth Minister, Changsha, Green Hill, Southern Gate, and Level Star—five, south at the top.

sentences.zh: 酒旗、天廟、東甌、器府、軍門、左右轄位於巳，其數六，西上。

translations.literal: Wine Banner, Celestial Temple, Eastern Ou, Arsenal Office, Army Gate, and Left and Right Regulators at si—six in number, ranked west at the top.
translations.idiomatic: At si: Wine Banner, Celestial Temple, Eastern Ou, Arsenal Office, Army Gate, and Left and Right Regulators—six, west at the top.

sentences.zh: 天相、天稷、爟星、天記、外廚、天狗、南河位於午，其數七；

translations.literal: Heaven's Chancellor, Heaven's Granary, the Torch Star, Heaven's Record, the Outer Kitchen, the Heavenly Dog, and the Southern River are stationed at wu; they number seven.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Chancellor, Heaven's Granary, the Torch Star, Heaven's Record, the Outer Kitchen, the Heavenly Dog, and the Southern River stand at the wu position; they number seven.

sentences.zh: 天社、矢星、水位、闕丘、狼星、弧星、老人星、四瀆、野雞、軍市、水府、孫星、子星位於未，其數十有三；

translations.literal: Heaven's Altars, the Arrow Star, Water Level, Que Hill, the Wolf Star, the Bow Star, the Old Man Star, the Four Waterways, the Wild Cockerel, the Military Market, the Water Office, the Grandson Star, and the Son Star are stationed at wei; they number thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Altars, the Arrow Star, Water Level, Que Hill, the Wolf, the Bow, the Old Man, the Four Waterways, the Wild Cockerel, the Military Market, the Water Office, the Grandson Star, and the Son Star stand at the wei position; they number thirteen.

sentences.zh: 自午至未，皆東上。

translations.literal: From wu to wei, all face upward toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: From wu through wei, all are oriented with their tops toward the east.

sentences.zh: 天節、九州殊口、附耳、參旗、九斿、玉井、軍井、屏星、伐星、天廁、天矢、丈人位於申，其數十有二，北上。

translations.literal: Heaven's Knot, the Nine Provinces' Diverse Mouth, Attached Ear, the Banner of Shen, the Nine Pennons, the Jade Well, the Military Well, the Screen Star, the Assault Star, Heaven's Latrine, Heaven's Arrow, and the Husband Star are stationed at shen; they number twelve, facing upward toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Knot, the Nine Provinces' Diverse Mouth, Attached Ear, the Banner of Shen, the Nine Pennons, the Jade Well, the Military Well, the Screen Star, the Assault Star, Heaven's Latrine, Heaven's Arrow, and the Husband Star stand at the shen position; they number twelve, tops toward the north.

sentences.zh: 天園、天陰、天廩、天苑、天囷、芻槁、天庾、天倉、鈇锧、天混位於酉，其數十；

translations.literal: Heaven's Garden, Heaven's Yin, the Celestial Storehouse, Heaven's Park, Heaven's Round Granary, Fodder Hay, the Celestial Granary Officer, the Celestial Granary, the Axe and Adze, and Heaven's Muddy Pool are stationed at you; they number ten.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Garden, Heaven's Yin, the Celestial Storehouse, Heaven's Park, Heaven's Round Granary, Fodder Hay, the Celestial Granary Officer, the Celestial Granary, the Axe and Adze, and Heaven's Muddy Pool stand at the you position; they number ten.

sentences.zh: 外屏、大司空、八魁、羽林位於戌，其數四；

translations.literal: the Outer Screen, the Great Minister of Works, the Eight Chiefs, and the Feathered Forest are stationed at xu; they number four.
translations.idiomatic: the Outer Screen, the Great Minister of Works, the Eight Chiefs, and the Feathered Forest stand at the xu position; they number four.

sentences.zh: 自酉至戌，皆南上。

translations.literal: From you to xu, all face upward toward the south.
translations.idiomatic: From you through xu, all are oriented with their tops toward the south.

sentences.zh: 哭星、泣星、天錢、天綱、北落師門、敗臼、斧鉞、壘壁陣位於亥，其數八，東上。

translations.literal: the Weeping Star, the Lamenting Star, Heaven's Coin, Heaven's Net, the Northern Falling Master-at-Arms, the Defeated Mortar, the Axe and Halberd, and the Rampart Formation are stationed at hai; they number eight, facing upward toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: the Weeping Star, the Lamenting Star, Heaven's Coin, Heaven's Net, the Northern Falling Master-at-Arms, the Defeated Mortar, the Axe and Halberd, and the Rampart Formation stand at the hai position; they number eight, tops toward the east.

sentences.zh: 內壝外眾星三百六十位，每辰神位三十自第二等以下，神位版皆丹質黃書。

translations.literal: Within the inner precinct and without, the multitude stars occupy three hundred sixty seats; for each chronogram thirty spirit seats from the second grade downward—the spirit tablets are all cinnabar ground with yellow script.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the inner sacred precinct, the multitude stars have three hundred sixty seats; for each of the twelve chronograms there are thirty spirit seats from the second grade down—all spirit tablets are cinnabar ground with yellow lettering.

sentences.zh: 內官、中官、外官則各題其星名；

translations.literal: For the inner officials, middle officials, and outer officials, each is inscribed with its star name.
translations.idiomatic: For inner, middle, and outer officials, each tablet is inscribed with the star's name.

sentences.zh: 內壝外三百六十位，惟題曰眾星位。

translations.literal: For the three hundred sixty seats outside the inner precinct, only the inscription reads “Seat of the Multitude Stars.”
translations.idiomatic: For the three hundred sixty seats outside the inner precinct, the inscription reads only “Seat of the Multitude Stars.”

sentences.zh: 凡從祀位皆內向，十二次微左旋，子居子陛東，午居午陛西，卯居卯陛南，酉居酉陛北。

translations.literal: All attendant seats face inward; the twelve chronograms turn slightly leftward; zi occupies east of the zi stair, wu west of the wu stair, mao south of the mao stair, and you north of the you stair.
translations.idiomatic: All attendant seats face inward; the twelve chronograms wheel slightly counterclockwise; zi stands east of the zi stair, wu west of the wu stair, mao south of the mao stair, and you north of the you stair.

sentences.zh: 器物之等，其目有八：

translations.literal: The grades of implements number eight in their categories:
translations.idiomatic: Ritual implements fall into eight grades:

sentences.zh: 一曰圭幣。

translations.literal: First, jades and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The first grade is jades and silks.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝蒼璧一，有繅藉，青幣一，燎玉一。

translations.literal: For the Lord on High of the Grand Heaven: one round dark-blue jade, with a crimson wrapper; one green silk; one jade for the fire offering.
translations.idiomatic: For the Lord on High of the Grand Heaven: one round dark-blue jade disk with a crimson wrapper, one green silk offering, and one jade for the fire offering.

sentences.zh: 皇地祇黃琮一，有繅藉，黃幣一。

translations.literal: For Imperial Earth: one yellow jade cube, with a crimson wrapper; one yellow silk.
translations.idiomatic: For Imperial Earth: one yellow jade cube with a crimson wrapper and one yellow silk offering.

sentences.zh: 配帝青幣一，黃帝黃琮一，青帝青圭一，赤帝赤璋一，白帝白琥一，黑帝玄璜一，幣皆如其方色。

translations.literal: For the associated lord, one green silk; for the Yellow Emperor, one yellow jade cube; for the Green Emperor, one green jade tablet; for the Red Emperor, one red jade tablet; for the White Emperor, one white jade tiger-amulet; for the Black Emperor, one black jade half-disk—all silks match their directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: For the associated lord, one green silk; for the Yellow Emperor, one yellow jade cube; for the Green Emperor, one green tablet; for the Red Emperor, one red tablet; for the White Emperor, one white tiger-amulet; for the Black Emperor, one black half-disk—and each silk matches its directional color.

sentences.zh: 大明青圭有邸，夜明白圭有邸，天皇大帝青圭有邸，北極玄圭有邸，幣皆如其玉色。

translations.literal: For the Great Brightness, one green jade tablet with a base; for the Night Brightness, one white jade tablet with a base; for the Celestial Sovereign, one green jade tablet with a base; for the Northern Pole, one black jade tablet with a base—all silks match their jade colors.
translations.idiomatic: For the Great Brightness, one green tablet on a base; for the Night Brightness, one white tablet on a base; for the Celestial Sovereign, one green tablet on a base; for the Northern Pole, one black tablet on a base—and each silk matches its jade.

sentences.zh: 內官以下皆青幣。

translations.literal: For inner officials and below, all use green silks.
translations.idiomatic: For inner officials and below, all offerings use green silk.

sentences.zh: 二曰尊罍。

translations.literal: Second, libation vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The second grade is libation vessels.

sentences.zh: 上帝大尊、著尊、犧尊、山罍各一，在壇上東南隅，皆北向，西上；

translations.literal: For the Lord on High: one great libation vessel, one presentation vessel, one sacrificial vessel, and one mountain jar—each one—set in the southeast corner of the altar, all facing north, ranked west to east.
translations.idiomatic: For the Lord on High: one great libation vessel, one presentation vessel, one sacrificial vessel, and one mountain jar—placed in the altar's southeast corner, all facing north, ranked from west to east.

sentences.zh: 設而不酌者，象尊、壺尊各二，山罍四，在壇下午陛之東，皆北向，西上。

translations.literal: Those set out but not poured: two image vessels and two jar vessels, and four mountain jars, east of the wu stair on the altar's south side—all facing north, ranked west to east.
translations.idiomatic: Set out but not poured: two image vessels, two jar vessels, and four mountain jars, east of the wu stair on the altar's south side—all facing north, ranked west to east.

sentences.zh: 皇地祇亦如之，在上帝酒尊之東，皆北向，西上。

translations.literal: Imperial Earth is the same, east of the Lord's wine vessels—all facing north, ranked west to east.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Earth follows the same rule, east of the Lord's wine vessels—all facing north, ranked west to east.

sentences.zh: 配帝著尊、犧尊、象尊各二，在地祇酒尊之東，皆北向，西上。

translations.literal: For the associated lord: two presentation vessels, two sacrificial vessels, and two image vessels, east of Imperial Earth's wine vessels—all facing north, ranked west to east.
translations.idiomatic: For the associated lord: two presentation vessels, two sacrificial vessels, and two image vessels, east of Imperial Earth's wine vessels—all facing north, ranked west to east.

sentences.zh: 設而不酌者，犧尊、壺尊各二，山罍四，在壇下酉陛之北，東向，北上。

translations.literal: Those set out but not poured: two sacrificial vessels, two jar vessels, and four mountain jars, north of the you stair below the altar, facing east, ranked north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Set out but not poured: two sacrificial vessels, two jar vessels, and four mountain jars below the altar, north of the you stair, facing east, ranked from north to south.

sentences.zh: 五帝、日月、北極、天皇，皆太尊一，著尊二。

translations.literal: For the Five Emperors, Sun and Moon, Northern Pole, and Celestial Sovereign, each has one great libation vessel and two presentation vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For the Five Emperors, Sun and Moon, Northern Pole, and Celestial Sovereign, each has one great libation vessel and two presentation vessels.

sentences.zh: 內官十二次，各象尊二。

translations.literal: For the twelve chronograms of inner officials, each has two image vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For each of the twelve chronograms of inner officials, there are two image vessels.

sentences.zh: 中官十二次，各壺尊二。

translations.literal: For the twelve chronograms of middle officials, each has two jar vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For each of the twelve chronograms of middle officials, there are two jar vessels.

sentences.zh: 外官十二次，各概尊二。

translations.literal: For the twelve chronograms of outer officials, each has two filtered vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For each of the twelve chronograms of outer officials, there are two filtered vessels.

sentences.zh: 眾星十二次，各散尊二。

translations.literal: For the twelve chronograms of the multitude stars, each has two simple vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For each of the twelve chronograms of the multitude stars, there are two simple vessels.

sentences.zh: 凡尊各設於神座之左而右向，皆有坫，有勺，加冪，冪之繪以雲，惟設而不酌者無勺。

translations.literal: Every vessel is set to the left of the spirit seat and faces right; all have stands, ladles, and added covers; the covers are painted with clouds—only those set out but not poured have no ladles.
translations.idiomatic: Every vessel stands left of the spirit seat and faces right; each has a stand, ladle, and fitted cover painted with clouds—only vessels set out but not poured lack ladles.

sentences.zh: 三曰籩豆登俎。

translations.literal: Third, baskets, beans, stands, and trays.
translations.idiomatic: The third grade is baskets, beans, stands, and trays.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝、皇地祇及配帝，籩豆皆十二，登三，簋二，簠二，俎八，皆有匕箸，玉幣篚二，匏爵一，有坫，沙池一，青瓷牲盤一。

translations.literal: For the Lord on High, Imperial Earth, and the associated lord: twelve baskets and twelve beans, three stands, two grain bowls, two grain vessels, eight offering stands—all with spoons and chopsticks—two baskets for jade silks, one gourd goblet with a stand, one sand pool, and one celadon sacrificial tray.
translations.idiomatic: For the Lord on High, Imperial Earth, and the associated lord: twelve baskets and twelve beans, three stands, two grain bowls, two grain vessels, eight offering stands with spoons and chopsticks, two baskets for jade silks, one gourd goblet on a stand, one sand pool, and one celadon sacrificial tray.

sentences.zh: 從祀九位。

translations.literal: Nine attendant seats.
translations.idiomatic: Nine attendant seats.

sentences.zh: 籩豆皆八，簠一，簋一，登一，俎一，匏爵一，有坫，沙池一，玉幣篚一。

translations.literal: Eight baskets and eight beans, one grain vessel, one grain bowl, one stand, one offering stand, one gourd goblet with a stand, one sand pool, and one basket for jade silks.
translations.idiomatic: Eight baskets and eight beans, one grain vessel, one grain bowl, one stand, one offering stand, one gourd goblet on a stand, one sand pool, and one basket for jade silks.

sentences.zh: 內官位五十四，籩豆皆二，簋一，簠一，登一，俎一，匏爵有坫，沙池，幣篚，十二次各一。

translations.literal: Fifty-four inner-official seats: two baskets and two beans each, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one stand, one offering stand, a gourd goblet with a stand, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set for each of the twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: For fifty-four inner-official seats: two baskets and two beans each, plus one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one stand, one offering stand, a gourd goblet on a stand, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set per chronogram, twelve chronograms in all.

sentences.zh: 中官百五十八，皆籩一，豆一，簋一，簠一，俎一，匏爵有坫，沙池，幣篚，十二次各一。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty-eight middle-official seats: each has one basket, one bean, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one offering stand, a gourd goblet with a stand, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set for each of the twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: For one hundred fifty-eight middle-official seats: each has one basket, one bean, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one offering stand, a gourd goblet on a stand, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set per chronogram.

sentences.zh: 外官位一百六，皆籩一，豆一，簋一，簠一，俎一，匏爵，沙池，幣篚，十二次各一。

translations.literal: One hundred six outer-official seats: each has one basket, one bean, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one offering stand, a gourd goblet, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set for each of the twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: For one hundred six outer-official seats: each has one basket, one bean, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one offering stand, a gourd goblet, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set per chronogram.

sentences.zh: 眾星位三百六十，皆籩一，豆一，簋一，簠一，俎一，匏爵，沙池，幣篚，十二次各一。

translations.literal: Three hundred sixty multitude-star seats: each has one basket, one bean, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one offering stand, a gourd goblet, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set for each of the twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred sixty multitude-star seats: each has one basket, one bean, one grain bowl, one grain vessel, one offering stand, a gourd goblet, a sand pool, and a silk basket—one set per chronogram.

sentences.zh: 此籩、豆、簠、簋、登、爵、篚之數也。

translations.literal: These are the counts of baskets, beans, grain vessels, bowls, stands, goblets, and silk baskets.
translations.idiomatic: These are the tallies of baskets, beans, grain vessels, bowls, stands, goblets, and silk baskets.

sentences.zh: 凡籩之設，居神位左，豆居右，登、簠簋居中，俎居後，籩皆有巾，巾之繪以斧。

translations.literal: Whenever baskets are set out, they are placed left of the spirit seat and beans to the right; stands and grain vessels center them and offering stands behind; all baskets have cloth covers painted with axes.
translations.idiomatic: Baskets are set left of the spirit seat and beans to the right; stands and grain vessels go between, offering stands behind; every basket has a cloth cover painted with axes.

sentences.zh: 四曰酒齊。

translations.literal: Fourth, wines and musts.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth grade is wines and musts.

sentences.zh: 以太尊實泛齊，著尊實醴齊，犧尊實盎齊，山罍實三酒，皆有上尊。

translations.literal: The great libation vessel holds thin first-ferment; the presentation vessel holds sweet rice wine; the sacrificial vessel holds thick brew; the mountain jar holds the three wines—all have upper libations.
translations.idiomatic: The great libation vessel is filled with thin first-ferment; the presentation vessel with sweet rice wine; the sacrificial vessel with thick brew; the mountain jar with the three wines—each has an upper libation.

sentences.zh: 馬湩設於尊罍之前，註於器而冪之。

translations.literal: Mare's milk is set before the libation vessels, poured into the vessel and covered.
translations.idiomatic: Mare's milk is placed before the libation vessels, poured into its vessel and covered.

sentences.zh: 設而不酌者，以象尊實醴齊，壺尊實沈齊，山罍二實三酒，皆有上尊，以祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Those set out but not poured: the image vessel holds sweet rice wine, the jar vessel holds steeped wine, and two mountain jars hold the three wines—all have upper libations—to sacrifice to the Lord on High of the Grand Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Set out but not poured: the image vessel holds sweet rice wine, the jar vessel steeped wine, and two mountain jars the three wines—each with an upper libation—for sacrifice to the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 皇地祇亦如之。

translations.literal: Imperial Earth is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Earth follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 以著尊實泛齊，犧尊實醴齊，象尊實盎齊，山罍實清酒，皆有上尊。

translations.literal: The presentation vessel holds thin first-ferment, the sacrificial vessel sweet rice wine, the image vessel thick brew, and the mountain jar clear wine—all have upper libations.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation vessel holds thin first-ferment, the sacrificial vessel sweet rice wine, the image vessel thick brew, and the mountain jar clear wine—each with an upper libation.

sentences.zh: 馬湩如前設之。

translations.literal: Mare's milk is set as before.
translations.idiomatic: Mare's milk is set out as before.

sentences.zh: 設而不酌者，以犧尊實醍齊，壺尊實沈齊，山罍三實清酒，皆有上尊，以祀配帝。

translations.literal: Those set out but not poured: the sacrificial vessel holds clarified wine, the jar vessel steeped wine, and three mountain jars clear wine—all have upper libations—to sacrifice to the associated lord.
translations.idiomatic: Set out but not poured: the sacrificial vessel holds clarified wine, the jar vessel steeped wine, and three mountain jars clear wine—each with an upper libation—for sacrifice to the associated lord.

sentences.zh: 以太尊實泛齊，以著尊實醍齊，皆有上尊，九位同，以祀五帝、日月、北極、天皇大帝。

translations.literal: The great libation vessel holds thin first-ferment and the presentation vessel clarified wine—both have upper libations; the nine seats are the same—to sacrifice to the Five Emperors, Sun and Moon, Northern Pole, and Celestial Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The great libation vessel holds thin first-ferment and the presentation vessel clarified wine—each with an upper libation; the nine seats share this rule—for the Five Emperors, Sun and Moon, Northern Pole, and Celestial Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 以象尊實醴齊，有上尊，十二次同，以祀內官。

translations.literal: The image vessel holds sweet rice wine, with an upper libation; the twelve chronograms are the same—to sacrifice to inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: The image vessel holds sweet rice wine with an upper libation; all twelve chronograms follow this—for inner officials.

sentences.zh: 以壺尊實沈齊，有上尊，十二次同，以祀中官。

translations.literal: The jar vessel holds steeped wine, with an upper libation; the twelve chronograms are the same—to sacrifice to middle officials.
translations.idiomatic: The jar vessel holds steeped wine with an upper libation; all twelve chronograms follow this—for middle officials.

sentences.zh: 以概尊實清酒，有上尊，十二次同，以祀外官。

translations.literal: The filtered vessel holds clear wine, with an upper libation; the twelve chronograms are the same—to sacrifice to outer officials.
translations.idiomatic: The filtered vessel holds clear wine with an upper libation; all twelve chronograms follow this—for outer officials.

sentences.zh: 以散尊實昔酒，有上尊，十二次同，以祀眾星。

translations.literal: The simple vessel holds aged wine, with an upper libation; the twelve chronograms are the same—to sacrifice to the multitude stars.
translations.idiomatic: The simple vessel holds aged wine with an upper libation; all twelve chronograms follow this—for the multitude stars.

sentences.zh: 凡五齊之上尊，必皆實明水；

translations.literal: For all five musts, the upper libation must be filled with clear water.
translations.idiomatic: For every grade of the five musts, the upper libation must be filled with clear water.

sentences.zh: 山罍之上尊，必皆實玄酒；

translations.literal: For mountain jars, the upper libation must be filled with dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: For mountain jars, the upper libation must be filled with dark wine.

sentences.zh: 散尊之上尊，亦實明水。

translations.literal: For simple vessels, the upper libation is also filled with clear water.
translations.idiomatic: For simple vessels, the upper libation is likewise filled with clear water.

sentences.zh: 五曰牲齊庶器。

translations.literal: Fifth, sacrificial meats and miscellaneous implements.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth grade is sacrificial meats and miscellaneous implements.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝蒼犢，皇地祇黃犢，配位蒼犢，大明青犢，夜明白犢，天皇大帝蒼犢，北極玄犢皆一，馬純色一，鹿十有八，羊十有八，野豕十有八，兔十有二，蓋參以國禮。

translations.literal: For the Lord on High, one dark-blue bull; for Imperial Earth, one yellow bull; for associated seats, one dark-blue bull; for the Great Brightness, one green bull; for the Night Brightness, one white bull; for the Celestial Sovereign, one dark-blue bull; for the Northern Pole, one black bull—each one; one pure-colored horse; eighteen deer, eighteen sheep, eighteen wild boars, and twelve hares—altogether blending in the national rites.
translations.idiomatic: For the Lord on High, one dark-blue bull; for Imperial Earth, one yellow bull; for associated seats, one dark-blue bull; for the Great Brightness, one green bull; for the Night Brightness, one white bull; for the Celestial Sovereign, one dark-blue bull; for the Northern Pole, one black bull—each one; plus one pure-colored horse, eighteen deer, eighteen sheep, eighteen wild boars, and twelve hares, blending the national rites into the whole.

sentences.zh: 割牲為七體：左肩臂臑兼代脅、長脅為一體，右肩臂臑、代脅、長脅為一體，右髀肫胳為一體，脊連背膚短脅為一體，膺骨臍腹為一體，項脊為一體，馬首報陽升煙則用之。

translations.literal: The carcass is cut into seven portions: left shoulder, arm, shank, and blade together with the short flank as one portion; right shoulder, arm, shank, short flank, and long flank as one; right thigh, shank, and ribs as one; spine with back skin and short flank as one; breastbone, navel, and belly as one; neck and spine as one; the horse's head, reporting yang and raising smoke, is used for that.
translations.idiomatic: The victim is cut into seven portions: left shoulder, arm, shank, and blade with the short flank; right shoulder, arm, shank, short flank, and long flank; right thigh, shank, and ribs; spine with back and short flank; breast, navel, and belly; neck and spine—and the horse's head, to report yang and raise the offering smoke, is used for that purpose.

sentences.zh: 毛血盛以豆，或青瓷盤，饌未入置俎上，饌入徹去之。

translations.literal: Blood and hair are placed in a bean, or a celadon tray; before the feast enters they rest on the offering stand, and when the feast enters they are removed.
translations.idiomatic: Blood and hair go in a bean or celadon tray; before the feast is set out they remain on the offering stand, and when the feast enters they are taken away.

sentences.zh: 籩之實，魚鱐、糗餌、粉糍、棗、幹橑、形鹽、鹿脯、榛、桃、菱、芡、栗。

translations.literal: Basket contents: fish paste, parched grain cakes, powdered rice cakes, jujubes, dried prunes, molded salt, venison jerky, hazelnuts, peaches, water chestnuts, gorgon fruit, and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: Basket offerings: fish paste, parched grain cakes, powdered rice cakes, jujubes, dried prunes, molded salt, venison jerky, hazelnuts, peaches, water chestnuts, gorgon fruit, and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 豆之實，芹菹、韭菹、菁菹、筍菹、脾折菹、裛食、魚醢、豚拍、鹿臡、醓醢、糝食。

translations.literal: Bean contents: pickled celery, pickled leeks, pickled smartweed, pickled bamboo shoots, pickled spleen, pressed grain, fish hash, pork hash, venison hash, fermented sauces, and scattered grain.
translations.idiomatic: Bean offerings: pickled celery, pickled leeks, pickled smartweed, pickled bamboo shoots, pickled spleen, pressed grain, fish hash, pork hash, venison hash, fermented sauces, and scattered grain.

sentences.zh: 凡籩之用八者，無糗餌、粉糍、菱、栗。

translations.literal: Where baskets number eight, omit parched grain cakes, powdered rice cakes, water chestnuts, and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: When baskets number eight, omit parched grain cakes, powdered rice cakes, water chestnuts, and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 豆之用八者，無脾折菹、裛食、兔醢、糝食。

translations.literal: Where beans number eight, omit pickled spleen, pressed grain, hare hash, and scattered grain.
translations.idiomatic: When beans number eight, omit pickled spleen, pressed grain, hare hash, and scattered grain.

sentences.zh: 用皆二者，籩以鹿脯、幹棗，豆以鹿臡、菁菹。

translations.literal: Where only two are used: baskets take venison jerky and dried jujubes; beans take venison hash and pickled smartweed.
translations.idiomatic: Where only two are used: baskets hold venison jerky and dried jujubes; beans hold venison hash and pickled smartweed.

sentences.zh: 用皆一者，籩以鹿脯，豆以鹿臡。

translations.literal: Where only one is used: baskets take venison jerky; beans take venison hash.
translations.idiomatic: Where only one is used: baskets hold venison jerky and beans venison hash.

sentences.zh: 凡簠簋用皆二者，簋以黍、稷，簠以稻、粱；

translations.literal: Where grain vessels number two: the bowl holds millet and panicled millet, the vessel holds rice and fine millet.
translations.idiomatic: Where two grain sets are used: the bowl holds millet and panicled millet, the vessel rice and fine millet.

sentences.zh: 用皆一者，簋以稷，簠以黍。

translations.literal: Where only one is used: the bowl holds panicled millet and the vessel millet.
translations.idiomatic: Where only one set is used: the bowl holds panicled millet and the vessel millet.

sentences.zh: 實登以大羹。

translations.literal: The stand is filled with the great broth.
translations.idiomatic: The stand is filled with the great broth.

sentences.zh: 六曰香祝。

translations.literal: Sixth, incense and invocations.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth grade is incense and invocations.

sentences.zh: 洗位正位香鼎一，香合一，食案一，祝案一，皆有衣，拜褥一，盥爵洗位一，罍一，洗一，白羅巾一，親祀匜二，盤二。

translations.literal: At the washing seat and principal seat: one incense tripod, one incense box, one food table, one invocation table—all with covers—one kneeling mat, one washing goblet at the washing seat, one jar, one basin, one white silk towel, two pouring ewers for the principal sacrifice, and two trays.
translations.idiomatic: At the washing seat and principal seat: one incense tripod, one incense box, one food table, one invocation table—all draped—one kneeling mat, one washing goblet at the washing seat, one jar, one basin, one white silk towel, two pouring ewers for the principal sacrifice, and two trays.

sentences.zh: 地祇配位咸如之。

translations.literal: Imperial Earth and associated seats are all as above.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Earth and associated seats follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 香用龍腦沈香。

translations.literal: Incense uses borneol and aloeswood.
translations.idiomatic: Incense is borneol and aloeswood.

sentences.zh: 祝版長各二尺四寸，闊一尺二寸，厚三分，木用楸柏。

translations.literal: Invocation boards are each two feet four inches long, one foot two inches wide, and three fen thick; the wood is catalpa or cypress.
translations.idiomatic: Invocation boards measure two feet four inches long, one foot two inches wide, and three fen thick; the wood is catalpa or cypress.

sentences.zh: 從祀九位，香鼎、香合、香案、綾拜褥皆九，褥各隨其方之色，盥爵洗位二，罍二，洗二，巾二。

translations.literal: For the nine attendant seats: nine incense tripods, nine incense boxes, nine incense tables, and nine brocade kneeling mats—each mat in its directional color—two washing goblets at washing seats, two jars, two basins, and two towels.
translations.idiomatic: For nine attendant seats: nine incense tripods, nine incense boxes, nine incense tables, and nine brocade kneeling mats in their directional colors; two washing goblets at washing seats, two jars, two basins, and two towels.

sentences.zh: 第二等，盥爵洗位二，罍二，洗二，巾二。

translations.literal: Second grade: two washing goblets at washing seats, two jars, two basins, and two towels.
translations.idiomatic: Second grade: two washing goblets at washing seats, two jars, two basins, and two towels.

sentences.zh: 第三等亦如之。

translations.literal: Third grade is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Third grade follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 內壝內，盥爵洗位一，罍一，洗一，巾一。

translations.literal: Inside the inner precinct: one washing goblet at a washing seat, one jar, one basin, and one towel.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the inner precinct: one washing goblet at a washing seat, one jar, one basin, and one towel.

sentences.zh: 內壝外亦如之。

translations.literal: Outside the inner precinct is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner precinct follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 凡巾，皆有篚。

translations.literal: For all towels, there are baskets.
translations.idiomatic: Every towel has its basket.

sentences.zh: 從祀而下，香用沈檀降真，鼎用陶瓦。

translations.literal: From attendant sacrifice downward, incense is aloeswood, sandalwood, and descending truth; tripods are pottery or tile.
translations.idiomatic: From attendant sacrifice downward, incense is aloeswood, sandalwood, and descending-truth resin; tripods are pottery or tile.

sentences.zh: 第二等十二次而下，皆紫綾拜褥十有二。

translations.literal: From the second grade and the twelve chronograms downward, there are twelve purple-brocade kneeling mats.
translations.idiomatic: From the second grade and the twelve chronograms downward, there are twelve purple-brocade kneeling mats.

sentences.zh: 親祀禦板位一，飲福位及大小次盥洗爵洗板位各一，皆青質金書。

translations.literal: For the principal sacrifice: one imperial invocation board, one seat for drinking the blessing and for the great and small rests at washing and goblet-washing—all green ground with gold script.
translations.idiomatic: For the principal sacrifice: one imperial invocation board, one seat for drinking the blessing and for the great and small rests at washing and goblet-washing—all green ground with gold lettering.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻飲福板位一，黑質黃書。

translations.literal: For secondary and final offering at the blessing-drink seat: one board, black ground with yellow script.
translations.idiomatic: For secondary and final offering at the blessing-drink seat: one board, black ground with yellow lettering.

sentences.zh: 禦拜褥八，亞終獻飲福位拜褥一，黃道裀褥寶案二，黃羅銷金案衣，水火鑒。

translations.literal: Eight imperial kneeling mats; one kneeling mat at the secondary and final blessing-drink seat; two yellow-way spread mats with treasure tables; yellow silk brocade table covers with gold; fire and water mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: Eight imperial kneeling mats; one kneeling mat at the secondary and final blessing-drink seat; two yellow-way spread mats with treasure tables; yellow silk brocade table covers with gold; fire and water mirrors.

sentences.zh: 七曰燭燎。

translations.literal: Seventh, candles and burning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh grade is candles and burning rites.

sentences.zh: 天壇椽燭四，皆銷金絳紗籠。

translations.literal: At the Heaven Altar, four rafter candles, all in gilt crimson gauze cages.
translations.idiomatic: At the Heaven Altar, four rafter candles, each in a gilt crimson gauze cage.

sentences.zh: 自天壇至內壝外及樂縣南北通道，絳燭三百五十，素燭四百四十，皆絳紗籠。

translations.literal: From the Heaven Altar through inside and outside the inner precinct and the north-south passages of the music enclosures, three hundred fifty crimson candles and four hundred forty plain candles—all in crimson gauze cages.
translations.idiomatic: From the Heaven Altar through inside and outside the inner precinct and the north-south passages of the music enclosures: three hundred fifty crimson candles and four hundred forty plain candles—all in crimson gauze cages.

sentences.zh: 御位椽，燭六，銷金絳紗籠。

translations.literal: At the imperial seat rafters, six candles in gilt crimson gauze cages.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial seat rafters, six candles in gilt crimson gauze cages.

sentences.zh: 獻官椽燭四，雜用燭八百，籸盆二百二十，有架。

translations.literal: Offering officers: four rafter candles; miscellaneous candles eight hundred; two hundred twenty grain-offering basins with stands.
translations.idiomatic: Offering officers: four rafter candles; eight hundred miscellaneous candles; two hundred twenty grain-offering basins with stands.

sentences.zh: 黃桑條去膚一車，束之置燎壇，以焚牲首。

translations.literal: One cartload of yellow mulberry strips, skinned, bound in bundles and placed on the burning altar to cremate the victim's head.
translations.idiomatic: One cartload of yellow mulberry strips, skinned and bound in bundles, placed on the burning altar to cremate the victim's head.

sentences.zh: 八曰獻攝執事。

translations.literal: Eighth, offering, regent, and attendant officers.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth grade is offering, regent, and attendant officers.

sentences.zh: 亞獻官一，終獻官一，攝司徒一，助奠官一，大禮使一，侍中二，門下侍郎二，禮儀使二，殿中監二，尚輦官二，太僕卿二，控馬官六，近侍官八，導駕官二十有四，典寶官四，侍儀官五，太常卿丞八，光祿卿丞二，刑部尚書二，禮部尚書二，奉玉幣官一，定撰祝文官一，書讀祝冊官二，舉祝冊官二，太史令一，禦奉爵官一，奉匜盤官二，禦爵洗官二，執巾官二，割牲官二，溫酒官一，太官令一，太官丞一，良醞令丞二，廩犧令丞二，糾儀御史四，太常博士二，郊祀令丞二，太樂令一，太樂丞一，司尊罍二，亞終獻盥洗官二，爵洗官二，巾篚官二，奉爵官二，祝史四，太祝十有五，奉禮郎四，協律郎二，翦燭官四，禮直官管勾一，禮部點視儀衛官二，兵部清道官二，拱衛使二，大都兵馬使二，齋郎百，司天生二，看守籸盆軍官一百二十。

translations.literal: One secondary offering officer, one final offering officer, one regent Minister of Education, one assistant presentation officer, one Grand Ritual Commissioner, two Palace Attendants, two Vice Presidents of the Chancellery, two Ritual Commissioners, two Directors of the Palace Department, two Directors of the Imperial Carriage Office, two Ministers of the Court of the
